## Offline / PWA (`app/manifest.ts`, `public/sw.js`)

The app installs as a desktop PWA and boots single-player offline after one online visit. `app/manifest.ts` plus the programmatic icons (shell section above) are the identity; `public/sw.js` — hand-rolled plain JS, no workbox/serwist dependency — owns offline caching:

| Request                                                                        | Strategy                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| navigation to `/`                                                              | network-first, cached shell as offline fallback; changed HTML re-precaches its static refs       |
| `/_next/static/*`                                                              | cache-first (content-hashed, immutable), insertion-order trim at 100 entries                     |
| manifest + icon routes                                                         | stale-while-revalidate                                                                           |
| everything else — `/api/*`, cross-origin, non-GET, RSC payloads, `/join/*` nav | **bypass, never touched** — the classifier's default, so online features can't be cache-poisoned |

- Install fetches `/` fresh and precaches every `/_next/static` URL parsed out of the HTML. All play-critical JS is statically imported from `/`; the one dynamic import (zzfx, gesture-gated — see Audio) is picked up by cache-first on the first online audio unlock, and missing it degrades to a silent game, never a broken one.
- `SW_VERSION` bumps only on cache-shape changes; HTML freshness never depends on it, which is what makes `skipWaiting`+`clients.claim` safe. Deploys apply silently on the next online load.
- Known bounded gap: going offline mid-re-precache leaves a broken offline boot until the next online visit — self-healing, and preferred over any stale-HTML scheme (those end in a purged-chunk 404 loop).
- `/sw.js` is served with a no-cache header (`next.config.mjs` `headers()`) and registered with `updateViaCache: "none"`; the pure `classify()` is exposed via `self.__sw` for unit tests (`tests/sw.test.ts`).
- **Dev invariant**: `components/ServiceWorkerRegistration.tsx` registers only in production builds; in development it actively **unregisters** service workers and deletes `monecraft-*` caches. e2e runs a prod build on `localhost:3000`, and a lingering SW would serve stale chunks to `bun run dev` on the same origin.

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, …) working in this repository. This file is the single source of truth — CLAUDE.md imports it.

## Project

A Minecraft-inspired voxel game: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), React 19, TypeScript (strict), Three.js, Bun. Single-player, browser-based, client-only, saves to localStorage.

**Zero binary assets**: every asset is generated at runtime — textures and sprites from pixel code, sound and music synthesized via ZZFX/WebAudio. New content should follow this principle unless the user decides otherwise. The one sanctioned exception is the UI pixel font (Monocraft, a Minecraft-style face under the SIL OFL 1.1), self-hosted via `next/font/local` from the committed woff2 in `app/fonts/` — don't "fix" it back to a system font.

## Commands

```bash
bun install        # Install dependencies
bun run dev        # Dev server at http://localhost:3000
bun run build      # Production build — part of the verification baseline
bun run lint       # ESLint (flat config, eslint .)
bun run typecheck  # next typegen + tsc --noEmit
bun run format     # Prettier --write (CI runs format:check — unformatted files fail the build)
bun test           # Unit + integration + component tests
bun run test:e2e   # Playwright browser smoke tests (needs `bunx playwright install chromium` once)
```

## Development Workflow

For a non-trivial change:

- **Branch only for big work.** A new feature, a large refactor or improvement, a dependency upgrade, or broad/risky work spanning many systems gets its own `<type>/<topic>` branch off `main` (e.g. `upgrade/next16-react19-three184`) so it lands as one reviewable unit. Minor work — bug fixes, small improvements, doc edits, single-purpose tweaks — commits straight to `main`, even when it touches a few files. Judge by scope and risk, not file count; when unsure, prefer `main`. Either way, the verify gate below must be green before anything lands on `main`.
- **Commit in focused slices.** One commit per logical slice (e.g. split a dead-code removal from the feature that replaces it). Keep `bun run lint` green at each commit so the branch stays bisectable. Use Conventional Commit messages; no `Co-Authored-By` trailers.
- **Explain the why in the commit body.** The subject says what changed; the body (separated by a blank line) explains why — the problem or motivation, and any non-obvious decision or trade-off. A body is required for anything beyond trivial edits (typos, formatting); `git log` should make sense without opening the PR.
- **Docs and tests ship _with_ the change — not later.** A change isn't done until the docs match it: the **Docs** section below says what each `docs/` file tracks, so update every page that covers what you touched — a `config.ts` tunable, a system, a mechanic, content, the save format — **not just the obviously behavioral ones** (a new tunable or a new test almost always has a companion doc that needs the same edit). Cover new logic with tests, keep the test coverage map current, and add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry. Flag any save-format or worldgen impact.
- **Verify before it lands** (before opening a PR, or before committing minor work straight to `main`): `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test`, and `bun run build` green (the same list CI's `verify` job runs); `bun run test:e2e` for changes touching the renderer, input, or React shell. A manual gameplay pass is only needed for pointer-lock handling or visual-appearance changes (see docs/testing.md). Then confirm the docs, tests, and `CHANGELOG.md` cover everything you changed (see the docs bullet above) — that check is part of the gate, not an afterthought.
- **Open the PR against this fork's `main`** (`gh pr create --repo hutusi/monecraft --base main`); do not add AI-attribution lines (e.g. "Generated with …") to the description. Pushing and opening PRs are user-authorized — don't push or open a PR unless asked.

## Docs

- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) — engine/renderer/audio/shell layers, step order, engine invariants & gotchas
- [docs/adding-content.md](docs/adding-content.md) — step-by-step: new block / item / recipe / mob / mechanic
- [docs/save-format.md](docs/save-format.md) — save schema, autosave, compatibility rules
- [docs/online.md](docs/online.md) — accounts/guests, cloud saves, invites, join tickets, env setup, local online dev
- [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md) — first-time deploy runbook (Vercel + Neon + Fly.io), shared secrets, verify, troubleshooting
- [docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md) — the client↔game-server wire protocol (framing, handshake, tick contents, close codes, trust model)
- [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) — test coverage map and the worldgen hash re-baseline policy
- [docs/tuning.md](docs/tuning.md) — gameplay tunables in `config.ts`, grouped by effect with balance trade-offs
- [docs/manual.md](docs/manual.md) — player guide (gameplay, survival, crafting, mobs, farming)
- [docs/reference.md](docs/reference.md) — gameplay reference tables (recipes, blocks, mobs, items)
- `README.md` — player-facing controls and quick start

Production still requires a real `DATABASE_URL`.

- **Optimistic block placement — building feels instant at any ping**: in an online world, placing a block now happens on your screen at click time instead of a full round-trip later (previously ~1.5 s of nothing at a 700 ms ping). The replica predicts only when it's certain the click is a pure block placement (right block in hand, nothing interactive or ridable in the aim) — every other right-click keeps its server-decided behavior; the command always travels and the server stays fully authoritative. Its block journal confirms the prediction, overrides it (you lost a race — the other player's block appears and your item comes back), or, if no answer arrives in time, the block quietly reverts with the item refunded. Your own placement sound/particles play once, at click time — the server echo is recognized (via the new event attribution) and swallowed.

2	
3	Three layers with hard boundaries:
4	
5	```
6	React UI (components/)          declarative HUD/panels; reads snapshots, sends commands
7	    │  useSyncExternalStore + engine commands
8	GameEngine (lib/game/engine/)   headless simulation: all game state, stepped per frame
9	    │  reads/writes
10	Voxel world (lib/world/)        data + generation + meshing + queries
11	    ▲  read every frame by
12	GameRenderer (lib/game/render/) Three.js: maps simulation state → GPU objects
13	AudioDirector (lib/game/audio/)  WebAudio: maps engine events + state → procedural sound
14	```
15	
16	The engine has **no React, no DOM, no rendering** — it runs (and is tested) headlessly in `bun test`. The renderer, the audio director, and the input controller are the only modules touching Three.js scene objects, the `AudioContext`, and DOM listeners respectively.
17	
18	The ONLINE layer (accounts, cloud saves, invites, join tickets) sits beside the shell: better-auth + Postgres behind `app/api` route handlers that adapt the tested rules in `lib/online/worldsService.ts` — see [online.md](online.md). Multiplayer adds a client session layer (`lib/net/NetworkSession.ts`, below) and a headless game server (`server/`, [protocol.md](protocol.md)) that both reuse this same engine. Offline single-player never touches any of it.
19	
20	## React shell (`lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`, `components/`)
21	
22	- `useMinecraftGame` creates the `GameEngine` in the canvas mount's callback ref, then an effect builds the `GameRenderer`, the `AudioDirector`, and `inputController` and drives the `requestAnimationFrame` loop: `engine.step(dt, input)` (in bounded catch-up substeps of ≤50 ms via `createAccumulator` from `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts`, so slow frames — e.g. software GL — don't run the simulation in slow motion) → drain engine events (death/respawn handling, `attackSwung` → `renderer.triggerSwing()`, + `renderer.handleEvent` for particle bursts, + `audio.handleEvent`) → `minimap.sync(state)` → `renderer.sync(state)` → `audio.sync(state, dt)` → `renderer.render()`. The minimap must sync **before** the renderer because it reads `state.worldMeshDirty`, which `renderer.sync` clears.
23	- `components/GameShell.tsx` is the menu shell **above** `useMinecraftGame`: a profile-select → world-select → play state machine (profiles own worlds; see [save-format.md](save-format.md)) that runs the one-time legacy migration on mount and renders `MinecraftGame` keyed by `world.id` (+ a reload nonce). Switching worlds, Load, or Reset changes the key, so React unmounts the game subtree — running the effect cleanup that disposes renderer/audio/input and clears the rAF + autosave — and a fresh mount boots the next world, **no page reload**. The tab's active world is remembered in `sessionStorage`, so a reload resumes it while a fresh tab cold-starts at the menu. `useMinecraftGame` therefore takes the `world` + `profile` to play and persists to that world's own `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key. **Cloud-linked worlds** (a `WorldMeta.cloudId`, set by the opt-in "Upload to cloud" action — see [online.md](online.md#worlds-invites-cloud-saves)) also mirror each local save up (`cloudSaves.pushSave`) and reconcile on open (`GameShell` → `pullCloudSaveIfNewer`, adopting the remote only when it advanced past this device's sync cursor); it's a local-manifest field, not part of the save format.
24	- UI state arrives as immutable `GameSnapshot`s via `useSyncExternalStore`; the engine replaces the snapshot object only when a visible value changes, so React re-renders are minimal and identity-driven.
25	- UI intents (`craft`, `swapSlots`, `selectSlot`, …) are dispatched as engine `Command`s. The only React state in the shell is pure UI concern: pointer lock, transient save messages, renderer failure.
26	- WebGL init failure is surfaced as `rendererError` and rendered as a fallback panel instead of crashing.
27	- On mount the shell installs a `window.__monecraft` debug handle (`{ engine, renderer, input, audio, net? }` — `net` is the live `NetworkSession` in online play) and deletes it on unmount. The Playwright suite in `e2e/` drives the game through this handle — asserting on engine state and `renderer.renderedTriangles()` rather than pixels (see [testing.md](testing.md)); it's also handy from the browser console.
28	- UI pixel art is procedural: `lib/ui/` generates 16×16 item/HUD sprites as pure pixel buffers (`spritePixels.ts`, `hudPixels.ts` — DOM-free, unit-tested) wrapped by a cached canvas→data-URL layer (`sprites.ts`, falls back to a transparent pixel under happy-dom). `chromeTiles.ts` (`installUiTiles`, idempotent, `document`-guarded) installs the GUI textures as CSS vars: the menu-backdrop noise (`--mc-tile-dirt/stone`) and the chrome grain layered over the flat panel/slot/button colors (`--mc-tile-panel/well/button`, which default to `none` so SSR/pre-install falls back to the solid color). No image assets, no licensing exposure. `lib/ui/` must not import Three.js or the engine.
29	- The installable app identity is procedural too: `app/manifest.ts` (name "Monecraft", standalone/landscape, theme colors from the menu gate's gradient in `menu.css`) plus icons generated from pixel code — `lib/ui/appIcon.tsx` paints an 8×8 grass-block face from `BLOCK_COLORS` as nested flex divs (Satori supports flex, not canvas/grid), wired through the `app/icon.tsx`/`app/apple-icon.tsx` file conventions and the explicit `/icons/{192,512,maskable}` route handlers the manifest references (file-convention icons don't auto-wire into the manifest).
30	- Item hovers use `useItemTooltip` (`components/game/ItemTooltip.tsx`): a cursor-following, `aria-hidden`, `pointer-events:none` tooltip portaled to `document.body` (so it never clips inside the scrollable inventory or blocks the pointer-lock click), replacing native `title=` on the hotbar, inventory, and recipe entries. Elements keep their `aria-label` for the accessible name.
31	- The one binary asset is the UI pixel font (Monocraft, a Minecraft-style face under SIL OFL 1.1), self-hosted via `next/font/local` from the committed woff2 in `app/fonts/` and exposed as `--mc-font`; the monospace stack stays as the fallback and on the F3 debug readout, and Monocraft's coding ligatures are disabled in `base.css`. This is the single sanctioned exception to "zero binary assets".
32	- Note for the React Compiler lint rules: consume the hook with destructuring (`const { … } = useMinecraftGame()`); property access on the result object can false-positive `react-hooks/refs`.

feat(pwa): offline app shell via a hand-rolled service worker

Single-player is already fully client-side; this makes it boot with no
connection after one online visit. public/sw.js is ~200 lines of plain
JS rather than @serwist/next: the repo is dependency-averse, Serwist's
plugin is webpack-era (a Turbopack risk), and the needs are small.

The Next+SW staleness pitfall is solved by never letting HTML freshness
depend on the worker: navigations to "/" are network-first (deploys
land normally; the cached shell is only the offline fallback), and a
changed HTML re-precaches the /_next/static URLs parsed out of it.
Static chunks are cache-first (content-hashed immutable). Everything
else — /api/*, cross-origin, non-GET, RSC payloads, /join/* — falls
through the classifier's bypass default, so online features can't be
cache-poisoned. The one dynamic import (zzfx, gesture-gated) is picked
up by cache-first on the first online audio unlock; missing it offline
degrades to a silent game, never a broken one.

In development the registration component instead unregisters workers
and deletes monecraft-* caches: e2e runs a prod build on
localhost:3000, and a lingering SW would serve stale chunks to
`bun run dev` on the same origin.

Verified against the prod build: install precaches the shell, manifest,
icons, font, and all 13 static chunks; an offline reload renders the
welcome gate; no /api entry appears in any cache.
EOF

content.content:
1	# Testing
2	
3	Two runners, three layers:
4	
5	- **`bun test`** — unit, integration, and component tests, colocated as `*.test.ts[x]` next to the code they cover. The shared setup (`tests/setup.ts`, preloaded via `bunfig.toml`) registers happy-dom so React component tests run under the same runner; the game engine itself needs no DOM (see [architecture.md](architecture.md)).
6	- **`bun run test:e2e`** — Playwright browser smoke tests in `e2e/*.e2e.ts` against the production build. The file suffix matters: `bun test` auto-collects `*.test.ts` AND `*.spec.ts`, so E2E files must use `.e2e.ts`.
7	
8	## What is covered
9	
10	| Area                          | File                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | What it pins down                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
11	| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
12	| Worldgen determinism          | `lib/world/generation.test.ts`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | SHA-256 digests of generated worlds per seed (the save-compat contract), plus structural probes, meshing snapshots, opaque/glass layer boundaries, thin door geometry, and dungeon presence — chests/spawners/mossy generate underground and `collectDungeonSites` reproduces every chest/spawner; plus per-world-type SHA-256 baselines (flat/amplified/islands) and shape probes (flat is level, amplified higher-relief, islands floods more with dry spawn land); **village** presence (houses build at each `collectVillageSites` center, the derive is deterministic, every center is clear of spawn) survives the re-baseline; **ocean flora** (kelp stands on sand under water, never breaches the surface-clearance band; coral sits on the floor), **shipwrecks** (fully submerged, a chest at every `collectShipwreckSites` index, derive deterministic), and **buried treasure** (a sand-capped chest in the beach band at every `collectTreasureSites` site, derive deterministic) — every generated chest belongs to a known dungeon/shipwreck/buried site                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
13	| Portable noise                | `lib/world/noise.test.ts`, `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts`                                                                                                                                                                                                           | The cross-engine determinism contract behind the worldgen digests: `portableSin`/`portableCos` track the true sine within 1e-6 across many periods, the hashes are uniform/axis-sensitive, and exact golden doubles are pinned; the e2e recomputes the full-size seed-1337 world digest inside Chromium/V8 and asserts it equals the Bun baseline in `generationBaselines.ts`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

53	| Browser E2E (multiplayer)     | `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | The full co-op journey on the real online stack (Next app on `pglite://memory` + the Bun game server — both booted by `playwright.config.ts`, zero external services): two isolated contexts register real accounts; the host signs up through the welcome gate's Sign in, creates an online profile and world through the account menus, and mints an invite; the friend registers on the `/join/<token>` landing page itself, then enters the joined world (labelled "Joined") from the account world list; both replicas see two players; a host block break reaches both block journals (the friend's journal is the wire proof — the host's own entry may be its predicted break); chat round-trips into both chat logs; the friend then digs under 400±100 ms simulated latency and the break must go through the prediction ledger locally (a rAF watcher catches the pending entry) while still reaching the host through the lagged link; the roster lists both players and only the owner renders a Kick control; then the owner kicks the friend, who lands on the disconnect modal while the host's player count drops to one; zero console errors throughout. (Arrow/vehicle replication stays on the unit tests — `server/room.test.ts` + `NetworkSession.test.ts` — as driving them end-to-end is too environment-fragile.)                                                                                            |
54	| Browser E2E (cloud saves)     | `e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts`, `e2e/accountSp.e2e.ts`                                                                                                                                                                                                               | A signed-in account's single-player cloud round-trip on the pglite stack, reached through the account home's "Local worlds on this browser" footer link: create a local world, place a distinctive Stone block in mid-air, Upload to cloud (the card flips to ☁ Synced), delete the local copy, clear this device's sync cursor (simulating a fresh device so the open-time reconcile adopts), then Download it from the Cloud Saves section — the placed block survives the push → delete → pull cycle. 56	
57	## Running the E2E suite
58	
59	```bash
60	bunx playwright install chromium   # once
61	bun run test:e2e                   # builds and starts the prod server itself
62	```
63	
64	E2E tests assert through `window.__monecraft` (the live engine/renderer/input handle — `net` is the session in online play; also handy in the browser console) instead of pixels; the one render check uses `renderer.renderedTriangles()`. The shared `gamePage` fixture seeds a default profile + world and enters it through the menu (reloads auto-resume the tab's world), then fails any test that logs a console error; `menu.e2e.ts` instead drives the menus from empty storage with the plain Playwright `test`.
65	
66	Playwright boots **two** servers (`playwright.config.ts`): the Next production build with a full online stack on an in-process ephemeral Postgres (`DATABASE_URL=pglite://memory` — no Docker; `db/index.ts` applies `db/ddl.ts` at boot) and the Bun game server (`PERSISTENCE=memory`) on port 18080. The offline suites never touch either backend; `multiplayer.e2e.ts` exercises both.
67	
68	**happy-dom has no 2D canvas context**: generated sprites degrade to a transparent data URL in component tests — assert sprite pixels in the pure `lib/ui` tests and component structure via roles/labels/`data-icon` attributes, not image sources.
69	
70	**happy-dom has no `AudioContext`** (and the `zzfx` package instantiates one at import): everything above the `SynthBackend` seam is pure and tested with a recording fake (see `audioDirector.test.ts`); the WebAudio glue itself (`synth.ts`, `musicPlayer.ts`, `rainLoop.ts`) plus real synthesis quality belong to the manual gameplay pass.
71	
72	**Known limitation:** headless Chromium cannot engage pointer lock (`requestPointerLock` never resolves). `acquirePointerLock` in `e2e/helpers.ts` tries the real thing, then falls back to forcing the input controller's lock flag — so key/mouse → engine wiring is still tested end to end, but real lock acquisition and look-around feel remain in the manual gameplay pass, along with visual quality. That manual pass is now only required for changes to pointer-lock handling or visual appearance.
73	
74	## The worldgen hash policy
75	
76	Saves store only the world seed plus block-change deltas, so `generateWorld` must produce byte-identical output for a given seed forever. The digests in `generation.test.ts` enforce that.
77	
78	**If a hash test fails after your change, your change breaks every existing save. Fix the code, never the hash.**
79	
80	Re-baselining the digests is legitimate in exactly one case: a **deliberate worldgen change** — flag it in the PR and CHANGELOG, and bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` so affected worlds discard their stale block-diffs (rebooting from their seed) rather than corrupting.
81	
82	To regenerate digests: temporarily log the computed hash in the failing test, run `bun test`, and paste the new values into `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` in the same commit as the cause.
83	
84	The digests are also an **engine-portability contract**: since worldgen v11, every seed-determined noise call uses the bit-portable implementations in `lib/world/noise.ts` (polynomial sine, integer hashes — only IEEE-exact operations), so the same seed generates identical bytes on every JS engine. `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` proves it in CI by recomputing the full-size world digest inside Chromium/V8 and asserting it equals the Bun/JSC baseline in `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` — this is what lets a browser client and a multiplayer Bun server share worlds by seed + block diff. `lib/world/noise.test.ts` additionally pins exact golden doubles of the noise primitives. New worldgen code must import its noise/trig from `lib/world/noise.ts`, never `Math.sin`/`Math.cos` (engine-defined per ECMA-262 — the reason the old digests were only valid on a pinned Bun).
85	
86	The **portable-noise worldgen (v10 → v11)** is the most recent legitimate re-baseline: same wave formulas on `portableSin`/`portableCos`, plus an integer-hash `hash2D`. All seven digests re-rolled; **every structural probe passed unchanged** — the polynomial sine tracks the real one within ~6e-8, so terrain structure is preserved and only scattered single-block flips (cobble speckle, cave edges, flora patterns) moved the hashes. This bump also retired the old "case 2" (a Bun version bump could shift `Math.sin` results): the CI Bun pin is no longer load-bearing for worldgen, though it stays pinned for plain reproducibility.
87	
88	The **deep-cave lava worldgen** was the prior re-baseline: the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v6 → v7. As with dungeons the structural probes (surface heights/biomes/snow/water) were left unchanged on purpose — `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` so it can't shift the ore→tree RNG stream, and the lava sits at or below `lavaLevel`, so the surface is byte-identical. A probe asserts lava is present and never rises above `lavaLevel`. Note the per-voxel **lighting** change re-rolled nothing: light is a derived runtime cache, never part of the generated bytes, and the meshing snapshot hashes only vertex positions — the new `aLight` attribute leaves them untouched.
89	
90	The **0.7.0 dungeon worldgen** was an earlier re-baseline: the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v5 → v6. The structural probes were left unchanged — dungeons are wholly underground, so the surface bytes are identical.
91	
92	## Writing new tests
93	
94	- Pure logic (inventory, spawn rules, a new system): unit-test the module directly.
95	- Gameplay behavior: boot a small engine — `new GameEngine({ seed, rng, worldSize: { x: 64, y: 150, z: 64 } })` — and step it with synthetic `FrameInput`. Inject a seeded `rng` (see `mulberry32` in the engine tests) for determinism.
96	- The world boots at dawn with hostiles nearby; use the `calmDaytime` pattern from the engine tests when testing unrelated mechanics.
97	- A ray origin exactly on a voxel boundary may target a diagonal neighbor (DDA ambiguity) — center positions in cells when aiming at specific blocks.

# Testing

Two runners, three layers:

- **`bun test`** — unit, integration, and component tests, colocated as `*.test.ts[x]` next to the code they cover. The shared setup (`tests/setup.ts`, preloaded via `bunfig.toml`) registers happy-dom so React component tests run under the same runner; the game engine itself needs no DOM (see [architecture.md](architecture.md)).
- **`bun run test:e2e`** — Playwright browser smoke tests in `e2e/*.e2e.ts` against the production build. The file suffix matters: `bun test` auto-collects `*.test.ts` AND `*.spec.ts`, so E2E files must use `.e2e.ts`.

## What is covered

## Running the E2E suite

```bash
bunx playwright install chromium   # once
bun run test:e2e                   # builds and starts the prod server itself
```

E2E tests assert through `window.__monecraft` (the live engine/renderer/input handle — `net` is the session in online play; also handy in the browser console) instead of pixels; the one render check uses `renderer.renderedTriangles()`. The shared `gamePage` fixture seeds a default profile + world and enters it through the menu (reloads auto-resume the tab's world), then fails any test that logs a console error; `menu.e2e.ts` instead drives the menus from empty storage with the plain Playwright `test`.

Playwright boots **two** servers (`playwright.config.ts`): the Next production build with a full online stack on an in-process ephemeral Postgres (`DATABASE_URL=pglite://memory` — no Docker; `db/index.ts` applies `db/ddl.ts` at boot) and the Bun game server (`PERSISTENCE=memory`) on port 18080. The offline suites never touch either backend; `multiplayer.e2e.ts` exercises both.

**happy-dom has no 2D canvas context**: generated sprites degrade to a transparent data URL in component tests — assert sprite pixels in the pure `lib/ui` tests and component structure via roles/labels/`data-icon` attributes, not image sources.

**happy-dom has no `AudioContext`** (and the `zzfx` package instantiates one at import): everything above the `SynthBackend` seam is pure and tested with a recording fake (see `audioDirector.test.ts`); the WebAudio glue itself (`synth.ts`, `musicPlayer.ts`, `rainLoop.ts`) plus real synthesis quality belong to the manual gameplay pass.

**Known limitation:** headless Chromium cannot engage pointer lock (`requestPointerLock` never resolves). `acquirePointerLock` in `e2e/helpers.ts` tries the real thing, then falls back to forcing the input controller's lock flag — so key/mouse → engine wiring is still tested end to end, but real lock acquisition and look-around feel remain in the manual gameplay pass, along with visual quality. That manual pass is now only required for changes to pointer-lock handling or visual appearance.

## The worldgen hash policy

Saves store only the world seed plus block-change deltas, so `generateWorld` must produce byte-identical output for a given seed forever. The digests in `generation.test.ts` enforce that.

**If a hash test fails after your change, your change breaks every existing save. Fix the code, never the hash.**

Re-baselining the digests is legitimate in exactly one case: a **deliberate worldgen change** — flag it in the PR and CHANGELOG, and bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` so affected worlds discard their stale block-diffs (rebooting from their seed) rather than corrupting.

To regenerate digests: temporarily log the computed hash in the failing test, run `bun test`, and paste the new values into `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` in the same commit as the cause.

The digests are also an **engine-portability contract**: since worldgen v11, every seed-determined noise call uses the bit-portable implementations in `lib/world/noise.ts` (polynomial sine, integer hashes — only IEEE-exact operations), so the same seed generates identical bytes on every JS engine. `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` proves it in CI by recomputing the full-size world digest inside Chromium/V8 and asserting it equals the Bun/JSC baseline in `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` — this is what lets a browser client and a multiplayer Bun server share worlds by seed + block diff. `lib/world/noise.test.ts` additionally pins exact golden doubles of the noise primitives. New worldgen code must import its noise/trig from `lib/world/noise.ts`, never `Math.sin`/`Math.cos` (engine-defined per ECMA-262 — the reason the old digests were only valid on a pinned Bun).

The **portable-noise worldgen (v10 → v11)** is the most recent legitimate re-baseline: same wave formulas on `portableSin`/`portableCos`, plus an integer-hash `hash2D`. All seven digests re-rolled; **every structural probe passed unchanged** — the polynomial sine tracks the real one within ~6e-8, so terrain structure is preserved and only scattered single-block flips (cobble speckle, cave edges, flora patterns) moved the hashes. This bump also retired the old "case 2" (a Bun version bump could shift `Math.sin` results): the CI Bun pin is no longer load-bearing for worldgen, though it stays pinned for plain reproducibility.

The **deep-cave lava worldgen** was the prior re-baseline: the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v6 → v7. As with dungeons the structural probes (surface heights/biomes/snow/water) were left unchanged on purpose — `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` so it can't shift the ore→tree RNG stream, and the lava sits at or below `lavaLevel`, so the surface is byte-identical. A probe asserts lava is present and never rises above `lavaLevel`. Note the per-voxel **lighting** change re-rolled nothing: light is a derived runtime cache, never part of the generated bytes, and the meshing snapshot hashes only vertex positions — the new `aLight` attribute leaves them untouched.

The **0.7.0 dungeon worldgen** was an earlier re-baseline: the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v5 → v6. The structural probes were left unchanged — dungeons are wholly underground, so the surface bytes are identical.

## Writing new tests

- Pure logic (inventory, spawn rules, a new system): unit-test the module directly.
- Gameplay behavior: boot a small engine — `new GameEngine({ seed, rng, worldSize: { x: 64, y: 150, z: 64 } })` — and step it with synthetic `FrameInput`. Inject a seeded `rng` (see `mulberry32` in the engine tests) for determinism.
- The world boots at dawn with hostiles nearby; use the `calmDaytime` pattern from the engine tests when testing unrelated mechanics.
- A ray origin exactly on a voxel boundary may target a diagonal neighbor (DDA ambiguity) — center positions in cells when aiming at specific blocks.

+- **Offline play (PWA, part 2)**: after one online visit, single-player boots with no connection — a hand-rolled service worker (`public/sw.js`, no workbox/serwist dependency) precaches the app shell and its static chunks, serves navigations network-first (deploys land normally and apply silently on the next online load), and **never touches** `/api/*`, the game-server connection, or invite links, so accounts, cloud saves, and multiplayer behave exactly as before. In development the registration component instead unregisters workers and clears caches, keeping `bun run dev` immune to a stale prod worker on the same origin. Pinned by classifier unit tests (`tests/sw.test.ts`) and an offline e2e (`e2e/pwa.e2e.ts`) that cuts the network and boots a world from the worker's cache.

- **Installable app identity (PWA, part 1)**: the app now ships a web-app manifest (name **Monecraft**, standalone landscape window, theme colors matched to the menu gate) and browser/install icons — an 8×8 grass-block face generated at request time from the same `BLOCK_COLORS` palette as the world atlas, via `ImageResponse` pixel code (`lib/ui/appIcon.tsx`), keeping the zero-binary-assets rule. The document title changes from "Minecraft Clone" to **Monecraft**, matching the in-game logo. Offline support (the service worker) lands separately.

- **Zero-config local dev**: `bun run dev` with no `DATABASE_URL` now falls back to an ephemeral in-memory PGlite database (with a one-time console notice) instead of 500-ing on the first online request — the full accounts/cloud-saves stack works out of the box in dev, resetting on restart. Production still requires a real `DATABASE_URL`.

- **Optimistic block placement — building feels instant at any ping**: in an online world, placing a block now happens on your screen at click time instead of a full round-trip later (previously ~1.5 s of nothing at a 700 ms ping). The replica predicts only when it's certain the click is a pure block placement (right block in hand, nothing interactive or ridable in the aim) — every other right-click keeps its server-decided behavior; the command always travels and the server stays fully authoritative. Its block journal confirms the prediction, overrides it (you lost a race — the other player's block appears and your item comes back), or, if no answer arrives in time, the block quietly reverts with the item refunded. Your own placement sound/particles play once, at click time — the server echo is recognized (via the new event attribution) and swallowed.

Production still requires a real `DATABASE_URL`.

- **Optimistic block placement — building feels instant at any ping**: in an online world, placing a block now happens on your screen at click time instead of a full round-trip later (previously ~1.5 s of nothing at a 700 ms ping). The replica predicts only when it's certain the click is a pure block placement (right block in hand, nothing interactive or ridable in the aim) — every other right-click keeps its server-decided behavior; the command always travels and the server stays fully authoritative. Its block journal confirms the prediction, overrides it (you lost a race — the other player's block appears and your item comes back), or, if no answer arrives in time, the block quietly reverts with the item refunded. Your own placement sound/particles play once, at click time — the server echo is recognized (via the new event attribution) and swallowed.

content.text:
Done — the PWA plan is fully implemented and verified on branch `feature/pwa`, four commits, nothing pushed (that's yours to authorize).

**What shipped:**

- `7ea8ccf` **Installable identity** — `app/manifest.ts` (standalone landscape "Monecraft", menu-gate theme colors), programmatic icons from an 8×8 grass-block face painted off `BLOCK_COLORS` via `ImageResponse` (zero binary assets holds), and the document title fixed from "Minecraft Clone" to "Monecraft".
- `7d8d9a7` **Offline app shell** — hand-rolled `public/sw.js` (~200 lines, no Serwist): network-first navigations with cached-shell fallback, cache-first hashed chunks, and a bypass-by-default classifier so `/api/*`, the game server, invites, and RSC payloads are never touched. Registration only in prod; dev actively unregisters workers and clears caches so `bun run dev` can't be poisoned by an e2e prod build.
- `5247ab6` **Tests** — 10 classifier unit tests pinning the "never touch /api" contract, plus an offline e2e: precache online, cut the network, reload from cache, boot a world, assert no `/api` entry in any cache. Also dropped the now-dead favicon-404 mute in the e2e fixture.
- `d205ac8` **Offline hint** — "Offline — local play only." on the welcome gate via a new `useOnlineStatus` hook; Sign in stays enabled.

**Worth knowing:** the maskable/apple icons initially rendered with hairline grid seams — Satori antialiases fractional cell edges, so the art scale must land cells on whole pixels (fixed with 0.625/0.8 scales, commented in the routes). And the plan's feared flake never materialized: Playwright's `setOffline` does cut service-worker fetches on current Chromium, proven by a `transferSize === 0` assertion on the offline navigation, so no fallback marker scheme was needed.

**Verification:** lint, typecheck, format:check, all 1203 unit tests (exit 0), build, and the full 24-test e2e suite — all green, with every existing suite now running service-worker-controlled as a non-interference regression. Docs updated throughout (architecture, testing, README, AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG).

**Left for you:** push + open the PR when you're ready, then the manual pass on the Vercel preview — Lighthouse PWA check, desktop Chrome install, a real offline session, and confirming a second deploy updates on the next online load.

gh pr create --repo hutusi/monecraft --base main --head feature/pwa --title "feat: installable PWA with offline single-player" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Makes Monecraft an installable desktop PWA: after one online visit, single-player works fully offline. Online features (accounts, cloud saves, multiplayer, invites) are untouched and the cache can never interfere with them by construction. Explicitly **not** mobile play — the game needs a mouse and pointer lock; that stays documented future work.

The codebase was already ~90% offline-ready (static `/`, zero network requests when logged out, self-hosted font, all art runtime-generated) — this adds exactly the missing PWA layer.

## What's here (one commit per slice)

- **Installable identity**: `app/manifest.ts` (standalone landscape, theme colors from the menu gate's gradient so the install splash blends into the first frame) + icons generated from pixel code — an 8×8 grass-block face painted from the same `BLOCK_COLORS` palette as the world atlas, via `ImageResponse` (zero-binary-assets rule holds; `public/` gains only code). Document title fixed "Minecraft Clone" → "Monecraft".
- **Offline app shell**: hand-rolled `public/sw.js` (~200 lines plain JS, no workbox/serwist — dependency-averse repo, and Serwist's plugin is webpack-era). Navigations to `/` are network-first (deploys land normally; the cached shell is only the offline fallback), changed HTML re-precaches the `/_next/static` URLs parsed out of it, static chunks are cache-first. Everything else — `/api/*`, cross-origin, non-GET, RSC payloads, `/join/*` — falls through the classifier's **bypass default**, so online play can't be cache-poisoned. In development the registration component instead unregisters workers and clears caches (e2e runs a prod build on `localhost:3000`; a lingering SW would serve stale chunks to `bun run dev`).
- **Tests**: `tests/sw.test.ts` pins the classifier contract (never touch `/api`, cross-origin, non-GET, RSC, `/join`); `e2e/pwa.e2e.ts` drives the real offline story — precache, cut the network, reload served from the worker's cache (`transferSize === 0` proves it wasn't an emulation leak), boot a seeded world, no `/api` URL in any cache. The favicon-404 console mute in the e2e fixture is dropped (there's a real icon now).
- **Welcome-gate offline hint**: "Offline — local play only." while offline, via a new `useOnlineStatus` hook; Sign in stays enabled (its failure copy is the real guard).

## Notes for review

- The one dynamic import (`zzfx`, gesture-gated for autoplay policy) isn't in the shell HTML, so install-precache misses it; cache-first picks it up on the first online audio unlock. Offline before that = silent game, never a broken one (`audioDirector` already catches the rejection and retries per gesture).
- Known bounded failure mode (documented in architecture.md): going offline mid-re-precache leaves a broken offline boot until the next online visit — self-healing, preferred over stale-HTML schemes that end in a purged-chunk 404 loop.
- Satori gotcha: scaled icon variants must land cells on whole pixels or the cell edges antialias into visible grid seams (commented in the icon routes).
- `SW_VERSION` bumps only on cache-shape changes; HTML freshness never depends on it.

## Verification

- Full gate green: `lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `bun test` (1203 pass, exit 0), `build`, and the complete `test:e2e` (24 passed) — every existing suite now runs service-worker-controlled, doubling as a non-interference regression.
- Docs updated with the change: architecture.md (new Offline/PWA section + shell-layer icon note), testing.md (coverage rows + SW note), README (install/offline blurb), AGENTS.md (`public/` holds code, not assets), CHANGELOG.

Still pending after merge: a manual pass on the Vercel preview — Lighthouse PWA, desktop Chrome install, a real offline session, and a second deploy updating on the next online load.
EOF

The candidate pool is already well-mapped from this session and the project memory: the #52 latency work explicitly named its own "next frontier" (combat lag compensation), the PWA plan parked mobile/touch and IndexedDB saves as documented future work, and a content batch has been the perennial runner-up.

My assessment of the four real candidates:

1. **Server-side lag compensation for combat** (my pick) — the one explicitly promised in the CHANGELOG ("combat at high ping remains delayed; that's the next frontier"). Your players genuinely split NA/Asia at 200–400 ms, and #52 fixed building/mining feel but not melee/bow. It's well-scoped: the server already owns hit results and stamps event attribution; this adds pose-history rewind on the server so a laggy player's swing is judged against what *they* saw. Medium size, high payoff for the actual player base.
2. **Mobile/touch play** — the biggest reach unlock and the natural sequel to the PWA (installable on tablets now, but unplayable without a mouse). Also the biggest lift: virtual joystick + look-drag, touch action buttons, UI scaling, replacing pointer lock. Large.
3. **IndexedDB save migration** — localStorage's ~5–10 MB quota is a real ceiling for long-lived offline worlds, and the PWA raises the stakes (offline players can't cloud-rescue a full quota). Infrastructure, invisible when it works.
4. **Content batch** — new blocks/mobs/mechanics via the documented `adding-content.md` pipeline. Keeps single-player fresh; endless scope, so it needs a curated slice.

I'm planning SERVER-SIDE LAG COMPENSATION for combat (rewinding entity poses when judging a high-ping player's melee/bow hits). Search breadth: very thorough. Answer each item with file:line evidence and short excerpts.

Trace: input controller → command dispatch → `routeDispatch` interception in online play (lib/net/NetworkSession.ts) → server room command handling → the combat system (lib/game/engine/systems/combat.ts or similar) → mob damage + `lastHitByPlayer`. Where is the hit target resolved, client or server, and against what positions?

2. **Bow/arrow flow**: where arrows spawn from a `fireBow`-like command, how the server simulates them (lib/game/engine/projectiles.ts, systems/projectileAI.ts), and whether arrow-vs-mob/player hits use current positions each tick.

What is the tick loop (server/room.ts? createFixedTicker in tickDriver.ts) — tick rate, tick counter, does the tick message carry a tick number or server timestamp? Cite the tick payload shape (lib/net/protocol.ts).

4. **What the client knows about what it's rendering**: the interpolation layer (lib/net/interpolation.ts) — remote mobs/players are rendered N ms in the past (adaptive 125–450 ms). When the local player attacks, does the client know which server timestamp/tick its rendered view corresponds to? Is there a clock-sync offset available (lib/net/clock.ts) with a getServerTime()-like API? Cite the APIs.

5. **Mob pose replication**: how mob positions reach the client (mp channel in the tick?), how mobs are identified across the wire (index? id?) — is there a stable mob id the client and server share? Same for remote players.

7. **Protocol versioning**: where PROTOCOL_VERSION lives, how a version bump refuses stale clients, and the total-validation pattern in lib/net/protocol.test.ts / protocol.ts I must extend if the attack command gains fields (e.g. a client view-timestamp).

8. **Existing tests to extend**: server/room.test.ts patterns (fake sockets, stepping ticks), lib/game/engine/systems/combat.test.ts (or wherever melee is tested), GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts — cite how a test drives a two-player room and asserts a hit.

9. **Config**: where gameplay/net tunables live (lib/game/config.ts? server config?) — attack range/cooldown constants, and any existing MAX_* clamps on client input the server enforces (applyRemotePose speed clamps etc.) that set the precedent for bounding the rewind window.

10. **Docs**: which sections of docs/protocol.md and docs/architecture.md describe the tick/combat/trust model (I'll need to update them); quote the trust-model bullet points about what the server never trusts.

I have everything needed. Here's the structured report.

---

# Lag-compensation research report — monecraft

Ground truth up front: **all hit resolution is server-authoritative and uses *current* (this-tick) positions.** The client sends only an `attack` intent plus its claimed eye pose; the server raycasts. There is **no server-side position history** yet — only last-sent "shadow" values for deadbanding and a command/pose replay log. The client *does* already compute a render timestamp on the server timeline every frame, but does not attach it to commands. Details per item below.

## 1. Melee hit flow today

The client sends a bare intent, not a target id and not a client-side raycast result. The **server raycasts against current mob positions**.

- Command type is parameterless: `lib/game/engine/commands.ts:34` — `| { type: "attack" }`.
- Input controller → dispatch: attack is dispatched as a plain `{ type: "attack" }` command through `engine.dispatch`, which routes via `routeDispatch`.
- `routeDispatch` interception (online): `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts:274-293`. For `attack` while online it pushes a **local cosmetic** `attackSwung` event (line 291 — "Swing feedback is pure cosmetics… hit results, damage, knockback stay server-owned") and then `sendCmd(command)` (line 292). Nothing about the target is computed client-side.
- `sendCmd` attaches the **claimed foot pose** (server adds `EYE_HEIGHT` itself): `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts:677-690` — `pose: { x,y,z,yaw,pitch }` quantized.
- Server room command handling: `server/room.ts:327-346` (`case "cmd"`). It re-applies the claimed pose through `applyRemotePose` (same clamps as the pose stream) so "the command's raycast happens from where the client actually stood/aimed" (lines 334-339), logs it to the replay ring buffer (line 343), then `this.engine.dispatch(message.cmd, playerId)` (line 344).
- Engine attack handler: `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts:923-948`. Emits `attackSwung`, branches to `tryFireBow` if a bow is held, else `tryAttackMob(...)` with `weaponDamage + strengthBonus + sharpnessBonus`, `weaponReach`, knockback, looting.
- Combat system + target resolution + `lastHitByPlayer`: `lib/game/engine/systems/combat.ts`.
  - `findAimedMobIndex` (lines 44-65) is where the hit target is resolved: from the player's eye (`position.y + EYE_HEIGHT`, line 46) along `lookDirection(yaw,pitch)`, it picks the nearest mob within `reach` **and** inside the aim cone (`scratchForward.dot(scratchToMob) < ATTACK_AIM_DOT` rejects, line 58). It iterates `state.mobs` using each mob's **current** `mob.position` (line 54).
  - `tryAttackMob` (lines 75-101): applies `mob.hp -= damage` and `mob.lastHitByPlayer = player.id` (lines 88-89, kill credit), knockback shove, and calls `onMobKilled` if `hp <= 0`.

So: **target is resolved on the server, against current mob positions, from the client's claimed eye pose.** The rewind you want would swap `mob.position` in `findAimedMobIndex` (and the projectile tests) for a historical pose.

## 2. Bow / arrow flow

- Fire path: `attack` with a held bow → `tryFireBow` (`GameEngine.ts:928-929`; `combat.ts:114-138`). It reads eye origin + `lookDirection`, calls `spawnArrow(...)` with `owner: player.id` for kill credit (combat.ts:124-131), consumes an arrow + bow durability, and arms `bowCooldownTimer = BOW_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` (line 135).
- Spawn: `lib/game/engine/projectiles.ts:25-47` — creates a `ProjectileState` with a stable numeric `id` (`state.nextProjectileId`, line 44), a muzzle offset, velocity = dir × speed, `fromPlayer`, `owner`, `ttl`.
- Server simulation each tick: `lib/game/engine/systems/projectileAI.ts` `tickProjectiles` (step order slot 12, `architecture.md:58`). Arrows integrate under gravity in capped substeps; per substep they sweep the world DDA for blocks and test the segment against entities.
  - **Player arrows vs mobs use current mob positions each tick**: loop over `state.mobs` reading `mob.position` (lines 71-92); on hit `mob.hp -= p.damage`, `mob.lastHitByPlayer = p.owner` (lines 113-115).
  - **Mob arrows vs players use current player positions**: loop over `state.players.values()` reading `player.position` (lines 94-105); on hit `deps.damagePlayer(...)` (line 127).
  - No history — the segment test is always against live `position`.
- Replication: arrows are broadcast in full every tick as `prj` (see item 3/5). Client snaps them per frame (no interpolation buffer) — `NetworkSession.ts:369-399`.

## 3. What the server knows about time / history

- **Tick loop:** `Room.tick(dt)` at `server/room.ts:396-463`, driven by `createFixedTicker` (`server/room.ts:174-179` → `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts:84-119`). Rate is **20 Hz**: `TICK_SECONDS = MAX_STEP_SECONDS = 0.05`, `TICK_RATE = 20` (`tickDriver.ts:18-23`).
- **Tick counter:** `this.tickCount`, incremented at `room.ts:398`.
- **Tick payload shape:** `TickMessage` in `lib/net/protocol.ts:168-187`. It carries `n` = **tick number** (line 169), plus `blocks?`, `ev`, `pp` (player poses), `mp` (mob poses, 10 Hz), `vp?`, `prj?`, `day?`, `self?`. **There is no wall-clock server timestamp** — only the tick number `n`. Built at `room.ts:428-439`.
- **Clock conversion:** client turns `n` into ms via `n * TICK_SECONDS * 1000` (`NetworkSession.ts:540`). The separate `pong` message carries `serverTick` for clock sync (`protocol.ts:194`).
- **Per-tick position history / ring buffers for rewind: NONE exist.** What the room keeps is:
  - `mobShadow` / `vehicleShadow` — `Map<id, {x,y,z,hp/…}>` holding only the *last broadcast* value for deadbanding (`room.ts:127-128`, updated 519-547 / 554-577). Current-only, not a timeline.
  - `commandLog` — a bounded ring buffer (`room.ts:146-147,214-217`, default 4096) of `CommandLogEntry` = a dispatched command with its claimed eye pose **or** a periodic pose anchor (`room.ts:101-104`; pose anchors every 20 ticks, lines 446-454). This is for *offline replay* (`GET /rooms/:id/log`, `server/index.ts:59`), not live rewind, and it stores poses only for players, not mobs.

Implication: implementing rewind requires a **new per-tick mob/player pose ring buffer** keyed by `tickCount`. The `commandLog` pose-anchor pattern is the closest precedent.

## 4. What the client knows about what it's rendering

The client already computes exactly the server-timeline instant it is rendering — it just doesn't send it.

- **Render time is computed each frame** in `afterFrame`: `NetworkSession.ts:805` —
  `const renderTime = (clock.ready() ? clock.estimatedServerTimeMs(nowMs) : serverTickTimeMs) - delayCtl.effectiveDelayMs(nowMs);`
  Remote players (806-814) and mobs (815-822) are sampled from their ring buffers at this `renderTime`. This is a **local const, not stored or attached to any outbound message** — sendCmd (677-690) does not see it.
- **Clock-sync API** (`lib/net/clock.ts:13-22`): `ClockSync` exposes `estimatedServerTimeMs(nowMs)` (server-timeline ms at local `nowMs`, NTP-style min-RTT offset, slewed), `rttMs()`, `ready()`, `onPong(...)`. This is your `getServerTime()` equivalent. Instantiated at `NetworkSession.ts:164` (`const clock = createClockSync()`), fed by pongs at line 614.
- **Interpolation delay API** (`lib/net/interpolation.ts:86-97`): `DelayController` exposes `effectiveDelayMs(nowMs)` (advances the slew) and `currentDelayMs()` (stat, no advance), plus `jitterMs()`. Delay is adaptive **125–450 ms** (`INTERPOLATION_DELAY_MIN_MS`/`MAX_MS`, lines 13-14). Instantiated at `NetworkSession.ts:165`ish (`createDelayController`), imported line 15.

So the exact quantity a rewind needs — "which server time was I looking at when I clicked" — is `clock.estimatedServerTimeMs(now) - delayCtl.effectiveDelayMs(now)`, already computed at line 805. To ship it you'd capture it at click time and add a field to `CmdMessage` (see item 7). Note the delay is *per-frame adaptive*, so the authoritative "view time" must be sampled at the click, not reconstructed server-side.

## 5. Mob / remote-player pose replication and identity

- **Mob channel:** `mp: MobPose[]` inside the tick (`protocol.ts:177`), collected in `collectMobPoses` (`room.ts:519-547`) at **10 Hz** deadbanded (line 528: `tickCount % 2`), with full **5 s keyframes** via `mobsKeyframe` (`room.ts:456-458`, `protocol.ts:189`).
- **Stable mob id shared across the wire:** `MobPose.id` (`protocol.ts:120`) = `mob.id`, a **numeric** id assigned from `state.nextMobId` at spawn (`systems/spawnDirector.ts:41,63`; also breeding.ts:58,83). The client upserts/looks up mobs **by this id**: `upsertReplicaMob` finds `state.mobs.find(m => m.id === pose.id)` (`NetworkSession.ts:401-402`), and per-mob interpolation buffers are keyed by `pose.id` (`mobBuffers.get(pose.id)`, lines 433-436, 555). Same id space server and client — good for rewind bookkeeping.
- **Remote players:** `pp: PlayerPose[]` (`protocol.ts:176`, 132-133), 20 Hz, collected in `collectPlayerPoses` (`room.ts:503-517`, own pose omitted). Identified by **string account id** (`PlayerPose.id`). Client keys `playerBuffers` by that id (`NetworkSession.ts:544-551`). `MobPose` also carries `kind/hostile/hp/moveSpeed`; `PlayerPose` carries `x/y/z/yaw/pitch`.
- Poses are quantized on the wire (`qPos` 2dp, `qAng` 3dp) via `lib/net/codec.ts` (used throughout `room.ts` collectors).

## 6. Prediction ledger precedent (`lib/net/prediction.ts`)

Shape you can mirror for swing/hit feedback (the docs already promise "instant swing feedback, hit results delayed" — `architecture.md:124`, "An `attack` plays its swing at click time … hit results stay server-owned"):

- `PredictionLedger` API (`prediction.ts:60-78`): 
  - **register** → `add(kind, edits, refund, nowMs, rttMs)` (81-97) — stamps a deadline via `predictionTimeoutMs(rtt)` (2×RTT+200, clamped 1000–5000 ms, lines 33-37) and sets an echo-suppress window.
  - **confirm / override** → `onJournal(idx, block)` (99-123) — a matching authoritative write confirms; a differing write drops the whole prediction, returns refunds + sibling `reverts`.
  - **timeout** → `expire(nowMs)` (125-129) — returns past-deadline predictions newest-first for revert.
  - plus `shouldSuppress(idx, nowMs)` (131-139, own-echo dedup), `clear()` (world-sync keyframe), `size()` (F3 overlay).
- Echo-suppression is the exact pattern already used for `attackSwung`: routeDispatch synthesizes the swing (`NetworkSession.ts:291`) and the inbound tick swallows the attributed echo (`NetworkSession.ts:574`: `if (ev.type === "attackSwung" && ev.playerId === playerId) continue`). A "hit feedback" ledger would extend this from swallow-only to predict-then-reconcile.

## 7. Protocol versioning + total-validation pattern to extend

- **`PROTOCOL_VERSION = 2`** lives at `lib/net/protocol.ts:20`.
- **Stale-client refusal:** the hello handshake in `server/index.ts:97-99` — `if (message.protocol !== PROTOCOL_VERSION) ws.close(CLOSE_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH, …)` and `if (!claims || claims.pv !== PROTOCOL_VERSION) ws.close(CLOSE_BAD_TICKET, …)`. The join ticket itself stamps `pv` (`lib/net/tickets.ts:28,86`). Bumping `PROTOCOL_VERSION` invalidates every ticket minted at the old number.
- **The command you'd extend:** `CmdMessage` (`protocol.ts:67`) already carries `{ t:"cmd", seq, cmd, pose }`; adding a client view-timestamp (e.g. `viewMs` or `viewTick`) is a field here, validated in `readClientMessage`'s `"cmd"` case (`protocol.ts:303-309`) alongside `readEyePose` (227-232). The doc comment at `protocol.ts:61-66` and the trust-model note ("the envelope already carries what stricter server-side rewind validation would need", `docs/protocol.md:125-127`) anticipate exactly this.
- **Total-validation pattern to mirror:** validators are hand-rolled and TOTAL (null, never throw) — `isNum/isBool/isStr` (211-213), `readMove`, `readEyePose`, `readCommand` allow-list (240-288), `readClientMessage` (291-321). The test that enforces it is `lib/net/protocol.test.ts`: "round-trips well-formed frames" (8-25, includes a `cmd`/`attack` case at 15-18), "rejects garbage totally (no exceptions, just null)" (27-44, includes a bad-pose cmd at line 38). Any new field must add a well-formed round-trip case **and** a garbage-rejection case here, plus you'd bump `PROTOCOL_VERSION`.

## 8. Existing tests to extend

- **`server/room.test.ts`** — the two-player room harness:
  - `fakeSink()` (20-39): a scripted `ClientSink` capturing frames, with `messagesOf("tick")` etc.; `bufferedAmount: () => 0`.
  - `makeRoom()` (47-52): in-memory persistence, `new Room(record, persistence, () => 0)` — **injected fixed clock** `now: () => 0`.
  - **Manual tick stepping:** `(room as unknown as { tick(dt:number):void }).tick(0.05)` (e.g. 98, 122) — no real timers.
  - **The exact melee-cmd precedent** to copy: "tick events carry the acting player's id" (112-130) drives `room.handleMessage("alice", { t:"cmd", seq:1, cmd:{ type:"attack" }, pose })` then ticks and asserts an `attackSwung` event with `playerId === "alice"`. A hit-registration test would add a mob and assert `mob.hp` dropped / `lastHitByPlayer`.
  - Speed-hack/forcePose precedent (132-150) shows how to drive poses and assert clamps.
- **`lib/game/engine/systems/combat.test.ts`** — melee/bow unit tests: `mobInFront()` helper (40+), `tryAttackMob` knockback/looting/`lastHitByPlayer` stamp (131-165), `tryFireBow` ammo/cooldown/enchant (66-131). A rewind-aware `findAimedMobIndex` would extend here with a "mob at a past position is hit" case.
- **`lib/game/engine/GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts`** — drives a two-player engine directly (`engine.addPlayer({ id: "acct-2" })`), asserts per-player kill credit ("kill credit follows the last player to hit", 169-189) and pose clamps ("under server authority, walking is pose-driven", 225-248 using `applyRemotePose`). Attack attribution at 150-168 (`engine.dispatch({ type:"attack" }, "acct-2")`).
- `lib/game/engine/systems/projectileAI.test.ts` covers arrow-vs-mob/-player hits (for bow lag-comp tests).

## 9. Config / tunables and existing input-bounding clamps

- **Combat/ranged constants** in `lib/game/config.ts`: `FIST_DAMAGE=6` (111), `ATTACK_REACH=4.5` (112), `ATTACK_AIM_DOT=0.89` (113), `MELEE_KNOCKBACK_IMPULSE=0.75` (114), `SPEAR_MELEE_REACH=7` (115); bow/arrow: `ARROW_SPEED=34`, `ARROW_GRAVITY=14`, `ARROW_TTL=4`, `ARROW_HIT_RADIUS=0.45`, `ARROW_MAX_SUBSTEPS=4`, `ARROW_MAX_SEGMENT=0.5` (127-132), `BOW_ARROW_DAMAGE=9`, `BOW_KNOCKBACK=0.6`, `BOW_COOLDOWN_SECONDS=0.4` (135-137). Player body: `PLAYER_HEIGHT=1.8`, `PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH=0.3`, `EYE_HEIGHT=1.62` (4-6). Movement ceilings used by the pose clamp: `SPRINT_SPEED=12.8` (10), `FLY_SPEED=11` (35), `JUMP_VELOCITY=8.2`, `GRAVITY=26` (7-8).
- **Cooldown gap to note:** there is **no server-side melee cooldown** — `tryAttackMob` has no rate check; only the bow has `bowCooldownTimer`. The only melee rate bound is the per-second **cmd flood guard `>= 60`** (`room.ts:328`). (`attackCooldown`/`attackTimer` at `state.ts:134-135` are **mob** fields, not the player.) If rewind lets high-ping players land more hits, you may want an explicit server melee cooldown alongside it.
- **The precedent for bounding a rewind window** is the pose-clamp elapsed cap: `MAX_REMOTE_POSE_ELAPSED = 0.5` (`GameEngine.ts:205`), applied in `applyRemotePose` (`GameEngine.ts:467`: `Math.min(Math.max(elapsedSeconds, 0.01), MAX_REMOTE_POSE_ELAPSED)`) with the rationale comment at 464-466 ("an unbounded gap … would inflate the speed ceiling"). Mirror this: clamp the client-supplied view-timestamp to a max rewind (e.g. tie it to `INTERPOLATION_DELAY_MAX_MS = 450` + RTT). The whole `applyRemotePose` clamp block (471-483: `maxHorizontal`/`maxUp`/`maxDown`) is the canonical "server never trusts client numbers blindly" pattern.

## 10. Docs to update (with the trust-model quotes)

- **`docs/protocol.md`:**
  - "Steady state" lists the tick payload: `tick { n, ev, pp, mp, vp?, prj?, day?, self? }` @20 Hz (lines 63-71).
  - **Trust model** (116-127) — the bullets you must revise. Quoting the "never trusts" content:
    > "The server is authoritative for the world: every gameplay command executes in ITS engine; clients cannot invent items or edits. The one client-owned thing is each avatar's own movement (clamped, never trusted blindly)." (118-120)
    > "Nothing a client predicts changes what the server accepts." (123-124)
    > "The claimed eye pose on `cmd` is the hybrid model's soft spot — acceptable for invite-only co-op, and the envelope already carries what stricter server-side rewind validation would need." (124-127) ← this is the explicit hook for your feature.
- **`docs/architecture.md`:**
  - Per-frame **step order** (44-59) — combat runs on the `attack` command, projectiles are slot 12 (58).
  - **Combat paragraph** (77): "Combat (`systems/combat.ts`) runs on the `attack` command rather than per frame: a held bow branches to `tryFireBow` … otherwise `tryAttackMob` swings."
  - **Multiplayer client** trust bullets (124-125): "Own movement is client-owned (the one hybrid concession) … the server clamps … and owns the consequences … Everything else is server-authoritative … An `attack` plays its swing at click time (the attributed echo is swallowed); hit results stay server-owned." And (125) the interpolation/clock description: "Remote entities render in the past — adaptively far … sampled at estimated-server-time minus an adaptive delay … `clock.ts` keeps the server-time estimate NTP-style."
  - `GameEngine` bullet (36) documents `applyRemotePose` as "the server-side gate on client-owned movement" and `routeDispatch` as the session intercept hook — both central to your change.

---

### One-paragraph orientation for the implementation
Add a `viewMs` (or `viewTick`) field to `CmdMessage` captured at click time from the render-time expression at `NetworkSession.ts:805`; validate it totally in `protocol.ts` + `protocol.test.ts` and bump `PROTOCOL_VERSION`. On the server, add a per-tick ring buffer of mob (and player) poses keyed by `tickCount` in `Room` (mirroring the `commandLog`/`mobShadow` style), clamp the incoming `viewMs` to a bounded rewind window (mirroring `MAX_REMOTE_POSE_ELAPSED`), and in the `"cmd"` handler (`room.ts:327-346`) temporarily resolve mob positions from history before `dispatch` — which means threading a "pose provider" into `findAimedMobIndex`/`tryAttackMob` (`combat.ts:44-101`) and the arrow entity tests (`projectileAI.ts:71-105`). Client-side hit *feedback* can reuse the prediction-ledger register/confirm/timeout shape (`prediction.ts`) and the existing `attackSwung` echo-suppression seam.
