- `engage`/`release` fire `onLockChange`; `forcePointerLock` doesn't; `clearKeys` drops everything; `dispose` cancels timer + listener
- visibilitychange while active → release + pause dispatch

### Slice 4 — `feat(ui): mobile viewport, safe areas, and short-landscape layout`
Files: `app/layout.tsx`, `app/base.css`, `app/hud.css`, `app/ui.css`, `app/menu.css`.
- `viewport` export (:15-17) → `{ themeColor, width: "device-width", initialScale: 1, userScalable: false, viewportFit: "cover", interactiveWidget: "resizes-content" }` (the anvil-rename text input opens a keyboard even with chat deferred).
- `base.css .game-root` (:55-61): keep `height:100vh;` then add `height:100dvh;` override line (graceful fallback for pre-15.4 iOS); same for `menu.css:356 min-height` and `hud.css:31 .pause-menu max-height`.
- Global `html, body { touch-action: manipulation; }` (kills iOS double-tap zoom despite the meta — the meta alone is NOT honored by Safari); `touch-action: none` goes on `.game-canvas-wrap` and later on the overlay classes. Do **not** put `none` on `.game-root` — effective touch-action intersects the ancestor chain and would kill panel scrolling (`overflow-y:auto` panels).
- `.game-root { user-select: none; -webkit-user-select: none; -webkit-touch-callout: none; }` (the text-selection callout is alive even though 300ms tap delay is dead).
- Safe areas: `.hud-bottom { bottom: calc(<current> + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) }`; `.minimap` top/right + insets; landscape notch: left/right insets on the (upcoming) joystick/action clusters — define the paddings now as CSS vars on `.game-root` (`--safe-l: env(safe-area-inset-left)` etc.).
- Height media queries: extend the two width-only blocks (`ui.css:902`, `:958`) to `@media (max-width: 720px), (max-height: 480px)` and add a short-landscape block shrinking `.pause-menu`/panel paddings. Desktop (height > 480, width > 720) stays pixel-identical — state that in the commit body.
Tests: none runnable meaningfully (CSS); verification = desktop visual pass + e2e suite green (catches layout-driven selector breaks).

### Slice 5 — `feat(ui): touch controls overlay wired into the game shell`
Files: `components/game/TouchControls.tsx`, `components/game/TouchControls.test.tsx`, `app/touch.css` (new, imported in `layout.tsx`), `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`, `components/MinecraftGame.tsx`, `components/game/InventoryPanel.tsx` (optional `onClose` X button), `components/game/InventoryPanel.test.tsx`.
- `useMinecraftGame`: read touch settings on mount (same effect as audio, :155-160); `const touchEnabled = resolveTouchEnabled(mode)` resolved once per controller build; renderer effect builds `createTouchInputController` or `createInputController` accordingly; expose `touch: { enabled, controls, sneakLatched }` + `engageControls` from the hook (controls surfaced via `useState` set with `queueMicrotask`, matching the renderer-error idiom at :285-287); `swapController()` for hot-swap (Slice 6 calls it); add `pointerdown` to the audio-unlock listeners (:314-316) — `touch-action:none` + pointer handling can suppress the synthetic `mousedown` the current unlock relies on.
- `MinecraftGame.tsx`: render `<TouchControls>` under the suppression condition (section 0); click-hint (:151) becomes "Tap to play" + full-area `onPointerDown={engageControls}` when touch is enabled ("Double-click to play" otherwise); hide `.caps-indicator` on touch; pass `onClose` to InventoryPanel (dispatch toggleInventory) — rendered for desktop too (pure win).
- `window.__monecraft.input` gets the touch controller when enabled (e2e uses `forcePointerLock`, still fine).
Tests: TouchControls component test with a mock `TouchControlsApi` — PointerEvent down/move/up on lookpad routes to `look*` with the right pointerId; joystick passes center-relative coords; jump/sneak/place/eat buttons call `buttonDown/Up`; Eat hidden when `showEat` false; unmount calls nothing unexpected (clearKeys is the shell's job via cleanup — assert the cleanup callback prop if you add one, or wire cleanup in `MinecraftGame` and cover in the hook's contract note). InventoryPanel test: X renders when `onClose` given, fires it.

### Slice 6 — `feat(ui): touch mode toggle + unstuck button in the pause menu`
Files: `components/game/PauseMenu.tsx`, `components/game/PauseMenu.test.tsx`, `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`, `components/MinecraftGame.tsx`.
- Options tab: "Touch Controls" segmented Auto/On/Off (`aria-pressed`, mode-option styling like the GameMode grid at :137-150); wires to `updateTouchSettings(partial)` in the hook (audio-settings pattern: ref + state + write + `swapController(resolveTouchEnabled(next.mode))`).
- Game tab: "Emergency Unstuck" button → `dispatch({type:"unstuck"})` + `resumeNow()` (helps desktop too; Shift+U has no touch path).
- Controls tab: append touch gesture rows (static strings) when touch enabled.
Tests: toggle renders/fires; unstuck button dispatches; hot-swap covered as a hook-level assertion via `window.__monecraft.input` identity change in the e2e (Slice 8) rather than a unit test (the swap lives inside the renderer effect).

### Slice 7 — `feat(ui): long-press item tooltips on touch`
Files: `components/game/ItemTooltip.tsx`, `components/game/ItemTooltip.test.tsx`.
Extend `useItemTooltip().bind()` (not a parallel system): add `onPointerDown` (only `pointerType !== "mouse"`): start `TOUCH_LONGPRESS_TOOLTIP_MS` timer → show at press point, set `longPressFired`; `onPointerMove` > slop cancels; `onPointerUp/Cancel/Leave` cancels timer; `onClickCapture`: if `longPressFired`, `preventDefault + stopPropagation` (so a long-press doesn't also swap slots/craft — recipe entries use `is-disabled` not `disabled`, so they will fire clicks); a document-level `pointerdown` (registered while visible) dismisses. Mouse path byte-identical.
Tests: long-press shows content; early lift doesn't; move cancels; the captured click after a long-press is suppressed; next pointerdown dismisses; mouse hover path unchanged.

### Slice 8 — `test(e2e): touch play smoke`
Files: `e2e/helpers.ts` (add a `touchMode` **option fixture**: `touchMode: ["off", { option: true }]`; when `"on"`, the existing `addInitScript` also seeds `minecraft_touch_v1` `{"mode":"on"}`), `e2e/touch.e2e.ts`.
```ts
test.use({ touchMode: "on", hasTouch: true, viewport: { width: 812, height: 375 } });
```
Note: Playwright's `hasTouch` does not flip `(pointer: coarse)` — forced `"on"` mode sidesteps detection entirely (and detection is unit-tested in Slice 1). The overlay is pointerType-agnostic, so `page.mouse` drives it (real PointerEvents with `pointerType:"mouse"`).
Test list (single serial spec, seeded-world fixture, `calmDaytime` first):
1. Overlay visible; "Tap to play" shown; tap → `__monecraft.input.pointerLocked === true`.
2. Joystick: mouse-down on joystick center, move 40px up, hold ~1s → `playerPosition()` changed.
3. Look: drag on lookpad 200px → `engine.state.player.yaw` changed by expected sign.
4. Hold on lookpad > threshold → `input.input.mineHeld === true`; lift → false. (Actually breaking a block: drag pitch down first, hold 2-3s, assert a block change — include if stable, else keep the mineHeld assertion; note in the spec comment.)
5. Place: `page.evaluate` puts dirt in slot 0, pitch down, tap Place → `itemCount` decreased.
6. Pause button → `engine.state.paused === true`, overlay unmounted; "Back to Game" tap → playing again (`pointerLocked` true — exercising `engage()` on touch).
7. Options toggle Off → `__monecraft.input` identity changed (hot-swap proof) and overlay gone; toggle On restores.
Also: existing desktop e2e suite must stay green (mode auto resolves off under `Desktop Chrome`).

### Slice 9 — `docs: touch play`
Files: `README.md` (:19 sentence → "Playable with mouse+keyboard or touch (tablets and landscape phones); touch play is v1 — chat and the debug overlay remain desktop-only."; Controls gains a Touch subsection), `docs/manual.md` (:44-45, :58-78 controls), `docs/architecture.md` (Input section: two controllers, one type, engage/release seam, the virtual-lock story), `docs/testing.md` (rows for touchSettings/touchInputController/TouchControls/ItemTooltip/touch.e2e), `CHANGELOG.md`, `AGENTS.md` (:32 manual-pass rule now: "pointer-lock **or touch-control** handling" + the device checklist pointer). Deferred list documented in README/manual: touch chat typing, F3, advancements button, keybinding customization, tap-a-block targeting.

---

## 4. Edge cases (implementation notes per slice)

- **Rotation/resize mid-play**: `GameRenderer` resizes via the window `resize` listener the desktop controller registers (`inputController.ts:204`); the touch controller takes no `onResize` — instead `useMinecraftGame` registers `resize` + `orientationchange → renderer.handleResize()` itself when touch is enabled (or unconditionally — simpler, one listener, harmless on desktop). Joystick origin is element-center computed per pointerdown (`getBoundingClientRect` at down), so rotation can't stale it. Active gestures across rotation: `orientationchange` → `controller.clearKeys()`.
- **Rapid-fire pause dispatch loop**: touch pause button = `release()` then `dispatch pause`. `release()` fires `onLockChange(false)` → shell `setLocked(false)` only — unlike desktop, no auto-pause is chained to it (that lives in the desktop `pointerlockchange` handler), so no double-pause.
- **Death/respawn**: hook already calls `input.clearKeys()` on `died`/`respawned` (:353, :362) — touch `clearKeys` drops gestures/latches/mineHeld; overlay is unmounted by `respawnSeconds > 0`, its cleanup calls `clearKeys` again (idempotent).
- **pointercancel** (iOS system edge-swipes, notification pull): every zone handler pair has a cancel branch = lift-without-action; the visibilitychange listener catches full app-switches.
- **iOS Safari gotchas**: double-tap zoom persists despite `userScalable:false` → `touch-action: manipulation` global + `none` on game surfaces is the real fix; text-selection callout → `-webkit-touch-callout: none`; `dvh` needs iOS 15.4+ (fallback line ships first); pinch-zoom is unblockable in-browser-tab via meta but IS blocked by `touch-action:none` on the touched element; safe-area insets require `viewportFit: "cover"` (Slice 4 ordering matters); `setPointerCapture` inside try/catch (also for happy-dom).
- **Hybrid devices** (iPad+keyboard, Surface): touch mode replaces the keyboard controller entirely in v1 — keyboard dead while touch is on; `off` mode restores it. Documented limitation.
- **Renderer**: DPR cap stays 2 (`GameRenderer.ts:126-129`); note in CHANGELOG/architecture: possible 1.5 cap + `RENDER_RADIUS` scaling as future mobile-perf work.
- **Audio unlock**: `pointerdown` added to the unlock listeners (Slice 5) — do not rely on synthetic mousedown.

---

## 5. Verification

Per-slice: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build`; `bun run test:e2e` from Slice 2 onward (input/shell touched). Desktop regression: the entire existing e2e suite is the guard that `locked` plumbing and pointer-lock behavior are unchanged.

**Real-device manual checklist** (only verifiable on hardware — run before merging the branch; iPhone Safari landscape, iPad Safari, one Android Chrome phone):
1. Auto-detection: touch controls appear with mode Auto on the device; do NOT appear on desktop.
2. Tap to play engages; first tap unlocks audio (hear footsteps/music).
3. Joystick 8-way walk; double-tap-forward sprints (hunger drains faster); knob visual tracks finger.
4. Look drag smooth at TOUCH_LOOK_SENSITIVITY — tune on device (the constant exists for exactly this).
5. Concurrent: walk + look + jump with three contacts; no stuck movement after lifting fingers in any order.
6. Tap attacks a mob; hold mines a block to completion; swipe-look never mines.
7. Place button places; Eat button appears with bread selected, eats; potion drinks.
8. Sneak toggle latches; flight via double-tap Jump in Creative; rise/descend while flying.
9. Hotbar tap-select; inventory open → X closes; craft via tap; long-press shows tooltip (recipe missing-ingredient info readable); slot long-press doesn't swap.
10. Pause → Options → touch toggle Off (controls vanish, hint reverts) → On; Unstuck button works.
11. Death → Respawn tap → tap to play again; no ghost mining after death.
12. Rotate device mid-play; app-switch away and back → paused, resumable.
13. No pinch/double-tap zoom in play; no text-selection callout on long-press anywhere on the HUD; no rubber-band scroll.
14. Notch phone: joystick/buttons/hotbar clear of the notch and home indicator (safe-area padding visible).
15. PWA install on iOS/Android; landscape orientation honored; offline single-player boots.
16. Perf spot check: playable framerate on a mid-tier phone; note FPS for the future DPR/radius knob decision.

---

## 6. Biggest risks

1. **Mobile GPU performance** (RENDER_RADIUS=90, DPR≤2): the game may be sub-30fps on mid phones — nothing in this plan fixes it; the manual checklist measures it and the DPR-1.5/radius knob is the named follow-up. This is the most likely "ships but feels bad" outcome.
2. **Hot-swap inside the long-lived renderer effect**: the `inputRef` refactor touches the hottest path in `useMinecraftGame`; the documented fallback (apply on next world entry) caps the risk.
3. **`locked` overload drift**: anything new that reads `document.pointerLockElement` directly instead of the controller breaks touch silently — the Slice 2 seam plus an architecture.md warning is the mitigation.
4. **Feel constants are guesses** until device testing (sensitivity, slop, hold ms) — they're in `config.ts` + tuning.md precisely so the device pass can adjust them without touching systems.
5. **happy-dom PointerEvent/setPointerCapture gaps** could force the TouchControls component test to stub capture — controller tests are DOM-free by design, so coverage of the logic doesn't depend on this.

# Mobile/touch play (`feature/touch-play`)

## Context

The PWA made Monecraft installable everywhere; lag comp fixed online combat feel — but the game is unplayable without a mouse. This adds touch play (virtual joystick, drag-look, action buttons) for tablets and landscape phones. Chosen by the user 2026-07-06 over IndexedDB saves and a content batch. **Merge gate: automated tests only** (user's call) — the real-device checklist is a documented post-merge fast-follow; feel constants live in `config.ts`/tuning.md precisely so device tuning needs no system changes.

The engine is already input-agnostic (verified): `FrameInput {move, mineHeld}` (`state.ts:442-455`) + `Command` dispatches + `engine.applyLook(dYaw,dPitch)` (`GameEngine.ts:1044`, pitch clamped there); ALL aiming is center-screen — zero cursor picking. Touch is an additive input layer, not a refactor. Zero touch/pointer/mobile code exists today; CSS is fixed-px with two width-only 720px breakpoints; `ItemTooltip` is hover-only; ~11 keyboard verbs need triage.

## Scope

**v1 (core play, tablets + landscape phones):** joystick move + PE-classic sprint (double-tap-forward-hold), drag-look, tap=attack / hold=mine on the look zone, buttons for Place/Jump/Sneak/Eat(contextual), top bar Pause/Inventory/Camera, hotbar tap-select (already works), inventory click-to-swap (already works) + an X close button, long-press tooltips, pause-menu touch toggle (auto/on/off) + Emergency Unstuck button, tap-to-play gate (no pointer lock), flight via double-tap Jump.
**Deferred (documented):** touch chat typing, F3, advancements button, keybinding customization, tap-a-block targeting, mobile perf knobs (DPR 1.5 cap / render-radius scaling), keyboard+touch hybrid simultaneity.

## Key decisions

- **Gesture model (PE-classic)**: tap on the free look area = one `attack`; press-and-hold within slop = `attack` + `mineHeld` until lift (mirrors desktop mousedown at `inputController.ts:168-172`); drift beyond slop = pure look drag, never mines. Mining stays on the look thumb so mine-while-aiming needs one finger; Place must be a button anyway (no right-click analog); Eat is a contextual button (`slot.hunger != null || slot.effect != null`), dispatching `eatFood`/`drinkPotion` per the KeyF rule (`inputController.ts:132-137`).
- **`engage()`/`release()` seam** (Slice 2, zero-behavior-change refactor): the `InputController` type gains these two methods; `useMinecraftGame`'s direct `pointerLockElement`/`exitPointerLock`/`requestPointerLock` pokes (verified at `useMinecraftGame.ts:354,368,444,451-453,524`) route through them. Touch then implements a **virtual lock**: `pointerLocked` reports an `active` flag, tap-to-play calls `engage()`, and the shell's `locked`-as-"is playing" plumbing (`MinecraftGame.tsx:140`, `ChatPanel.tsx:63`) works unchanged. `forcePointerLock` sets `active` silently → `e2e/helpers.ts` untouched.
- **Controller/overlay split**: `lib/game/input/touchInputController.ts` (DOM-free except `visibilitychange`→release+pause, the touch analog of lock-loss-pause; injectable now/schedule/cancel for deterministic tests) owns FrameInput mutation/applyLook/dispatch/gesture state machine; `components/game/TouchControls.tsx` is dumb rendering + Pointer Events forwarding `{pointerId,x,y}` (pointerType-agnostic so `page.mouse` drives it in e2e; `setPointerCapture` in try/catch). Overlay unmounts whenever a panel/death/pause is up; cleanup calls `clearKeys()`.
- **Mode**: `auto | on | off` in `lib/game/input/touchSettings.ts` (audio-settings pattern, key `minecraft_touch_v1`); auto = `(pointer: coarse)` && `maxTouchPoints > 0`; PauseMenu Options toggle; **hot-swap** via an `inputRef` + `swapController()` (fallback if the effect lifecycle fights back: apply on next world entry — decide in-branch, note in PR).
- **Constants** (config.ts, tuning.md "Touch feel" section): `TOUCH_LOOK_SENSITIVITY 0.0042` (2× mouse — thumb travel is short), `TOUCH_TAP_MAX_MS 220`, `TOUCH_TAP_SLOP_PX 12`, `TOUCH_HOLD_MINE_MS 220` (= TAP_MAX, no ambiguity gap), `TOUCH_JOYSTICK_RADIUS_PX 64`, `TOUCH_JOYSTICK_DEADZONE 0.18`, `TOUCH_SPRINT_DOUBLE_TAP_MS 300`, `TOUCH_LONGPRESS_TOOLTIP_MS 450`. Joystick: 8-way sectors via `DIAG = sin(π/8)` on the normalized vector; deadzone zeroes intents. Flight double-tap reuses `FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS`.
- **iOS realities** (Slice 4): `userScalable:false` alone does NOT stop double-tap zoom — global `touch-action: manipulation` + `none` on game surfaces is the real fix (NOT on `.game-root` — effective touch-action intersects ancestors and would kill panel scrolling); `-webkit-touch-callout: none`; `100dvh` as an override line after `100vh` (iOS 15.4+ with fallback); safe-areas need `viewportFit: "cover"` + `env(safe-area-inset-*)` vars; `interactiveWidget: "resizes-content"` (anvil rename input opens a keyboard).
- **Desktop stays pixel- and behavior-identical**: height-based media queries only add below 480px height; Slice 2 is refactor-only; the full existing e2e suite is the desktop regression guard.

## Slices (branch `feature/touch-play` off main)

1. **`feat(input): touch settings with auto device detection`** — `touchSettings.ts` (+test): read/write/validate (injectable storage + window-shaped `{matchMedia, navigator}`), `resolveTouchEnabled(mode)`.
2. **`refactor(input): engage/release seam on InputController`** — extend the type + desktop impl (`engage` = current :451-453 body; `release` = exit-if-canvas-holds-lock); reroute `useMinecraftGame` :354/:368/:444/:524; introduce `inputRef` (rAF reads `inputRef.current.input` at :340). Zero behavior change; desktop e2e green is the gate.
3. **`feat(input): touch input controller`** — `touchInputController.ts` (+test, stub engine + fake clock): joystick math, sprint latch, look/tap/hold/cancel state machine, jump double-tap flight, gates (`active` && !`uiBlocked`), visibilitychange→release+pause, clearKeys/dispose. Constants into config.ts + tuning.md.
4. **`feat(ui): mobile viewport, safe areas, and short-landscape layout`** — layout.tsx viewport fields; base/hud/ui/menu.css: touch-action, callout/user-select, dvh overrides, safe-area vars + hud-bottom/minimap insets, extend the 720px blocks to `(max-width:720px), (max-height:480px)` + a short-landscape panel-padding block.
5. **`feat(ui): touch controls overlay wired into the game shell`** — `TouchControls.tsx` (+test with mock api), `app/touch.css`; `useMinecraftGame`: settings load, controller pick, `touch` + `engageControls` exposure, `pointerdown` added to audio-unlock listeners (:314-316); `MinecraftGame.tsx`: overlay under the suppression condition, "Tap to play" hint variant with full-area engage, hide caps-indicator on touch; `InventoryPanel` gains an optional X close (desktop too; +test).
6. **`feat(ui): touch mode toggle + unstuck button in the pause menu`** — Options segmented Auto/On/Off; Game tab Emergency Unstuck (`unstuck` + resume — helps desktop too); Controls tab touch gesture rows; hook `updateTouchSettings` + `swapController`. (+PauseMenu tests)
7. **`feat(ui): long-press item tooltips on touch`** — extend `useItemTooltip().bind()`: pointerdown (non-mouse) starts a 450 ms timer → show anchored; move>slop/up/cancel cancels; `onClickCapture` suppresses the post-long-press click (recipe entries use `is-disabled`, they DO fire clicks); document pointerdown dismisses. Mouse path byte-identical. (+tests)
8. **`test(e2e): touch play smoke`** — helpers gain a `touchMode` option fixture seeding `minecraft_touch_v1` (Playwright `hasTouch` doesn't flip `pointer: coarse` — forced mode sidesteps detection, which Slice 1 unit-covers); `e2e/touch.e2e.ts` with `test.use({ touchMode:"on", hasTouch:true, viewport:{812×375} })`: tap-to-play → virtual lock; joystick moves the player; drag changes yaw; hold sets `mineHeld` (real block break if stable); Place consumes an item; Pause→resume exercises touch `engage()`; Options toggle proves the hot-swap (`__monecraft.input` identity change). Desktop suite must stay green.
9. **`docs: touch play`** — README (revise `:19` "Not a mobile game…" + Touch controls subsection), manual.md controls, architecture.md input section (two controllers, one type, virtual-lock story, warning: never read `pointerLockElement` directly — use the seam), testing.md rows, CHANGELOG, AGENTS.md manual-pass rule (+ touch-control changes) + the device checklist location.

## Edge cases
Rotation: joystick origin computed per pointerdown; `orientationchange` → `renderer.handleResize()` + `clearKeys()` (register in the hook, harmless on desktop). Death/station events already `clearKeys()` (:353/:362); overlay unmount repeats it (idempotent). `pointercancel` everywhere = lift-without-action. Touch pause = `release()` then `dispatch pause` — no double-pause (auto-pause-on-lock-loss is desktop-only). Hybrid keyboard+touch: touch mode replaces keyboard in v1 (documented; `off` restores).

## Verification
- Per slice: `bun run format` + `lint` (per-commit gate); full gate (typecheck, format:check, bun test, build) + full `test:e2e` before the PR (port 3000 lsof check first).
- **Merge gate = automated only** (user decision 2026-07-06). The 16-item real-device checklist (iPhone Safari landscape, iPad, Android Chrome: detection, audio unlock, 3-contact concurrency, gesture discrimination, safe-areas, no zoom/callout, rotation, app-switch, PWA install, perf spot-check) ships in the PR description as the named fast-follow; feel-constant tuning lands as a config-only follow-up commit.
- Known risk ranking: mobile GPU perf (measure on device; DPR/radius knobs are named future work) > hot-swap-in-effect (fallback: apply on re-entry) > `locked` drift (architecture.md warning) > feel constants (config-only tuning).

## Reused existing code

# Mobile/touch play (`feature/touch-play`)

## Context

The PWA made Monecraft installable everywhere; lag comp fixed online combat feel — but the game is unplayable without a mouse. This adds touch play (virtual joystick, drag-look, action buttons) for tablets and landscape phones. Chosen by the user 2026-07-06 over IndexedDB saves and a content batch. **Merge gate: automated tests only** (user's call) — the real-device checklist is a documented post-merge fast-follow; feel constants live in `config.ts`/tuning.md precisely so device tuning needs no system changes.

The engine is already input-agnostic (verified): `FrameInput {move, mineHeld}` (`state.ts:442-455`) + `Command` dispatches + `engine.applyLook(dYaw,dPitch)` (`GameEngine.ts:1044`, pitch clamped there); ALL aiming is center-screen — zero cursor picking. Touch is an additive input layer, not a refactor. Zero touch/pointer/mobile code exists today; CSS is fixed-px with two width-only 720px breakpoints; `ItemTooltip` is hover-only; ~11 keyboard verbs need triage.

## Scope

**v1 (core play, tablets + landscape phones):** joystick move + PE-classic sprint (double-tap-forward-hold), drag-look, tap=attack / hold=mine on the look zone, buttons for Place/Jump/Sneak/Eat(contextual), top bar Pause/Inventory/Camera, hotbar tap-select (already works), inventory click-to-swap (already works) + an X close button, long-press tooltips, pause-menu touch toggle (auto/on/off) + Emergency Unstuck button, tap-to-play gate (no pointer lock), flight via double-tap Jump.
**Deferred (documented):** touch chat typing, F3, advancements button, keybinding customization, tap-a-block targeting, mobile perf knobs (DPR 1.5 cap / render-radius scaling), keyboard+touch hybrid simultaneity.

## Key decisions

- **Gesture model (PE-classic)**: tap on the free look area = one `attack`; press-and-hold within slop = `attack` + `mineHeld` until lift (mirrors desktop mousedown at `inputController.ts:168-172`); drift beyond slop = pure look drag, never mines. Mining stays on the look thumb so mine-while-aiming needs one finger; Place must be a button anyway (no right-click analog); Eat is a contextual button (`slot.hunger != null || slot.effect != null`), dispatching `eatFood`/`drinkPotion` per the KeyF rule (`inputController.ts:132-137`).
- **`engage()`/`release()` seam** (Slice 2, zero-behavior-change refactor): the `InputController` type gains these two methods; `useMinecraftGame`'s direct `pointerLockElement`/`exitPointerLock`/`requestPointerLock` pokes (verified at `useMinecraftGame.ts:354,368,444,451-453,524`) route through them. Touch then implements a **virtual lock**: `pointerLocked` reports an `active` flag, tap-to-play calls `engage()`, and the shell's `locked`-as-"is playing" plumbing (`MinecraftGame.tsx:140`, `ChatPanel.tsx:63`) works unchanged. `forcePointerLock` sets `active` silently → `e2e/helpers.ts` untouched.
- **Controller/overlay split**: `lib/game/input/touchInputController.ts` (DOM-free except `visibilitychange`→release+pause, the touch analog of lock-loss-pause; injectable now/schedule/cancel for deterministic tests) owns FrameInput mutation/applyLook/dispatch/gesture state machine; `components/game/TouchControls.tsx` is dumb rendering + Pointer Events forwarding `{pointerId,x,y}` (pointerType-agnostic so `page.mouse` drives it in e2e; `setPointerCapture` in try/catch). Overlay unmounts whenever a panel/death/pause is up; cleanup calls `clearKeys()`.
- **Mode**: `auto | on | off` in `lib/game/input/touchSettings.ts` (audio-settings pattern, key `minecraft_touch_v1`); auto = `(pointer: coarse)` && `maxTouchPoints > 0`; PauseMenu Options toggle; **hot-swap** via an `inputRef` + `swapController()` (fallback if the effect lifecycle fights back: apply on next world entry — decide in-branch, note in PR).
- **Constants** (config.ts, tuning.md "Touch feel" section): `TOUCH_LOOK_SENSITIVITY 0.0042` (2× mouse — thumb travel is short), `TOUCH_TAP_MAX_MS 220`, `TOUCH_TAP_SLOP_PX 12`, `TOUCH_HOLD_MINE_MS 220` (= TAP_MAX, no ambiguity gap), `TOUCH_JOYSTICK_RADIUS_PX 64`, `TOUCH_JOYSTICK_DEADZONE 0.18`, `TOUCH_SPRINT_DOUBLE_TAP_MS 300`, `TOUCH_LONGPRESS_TOOLTIP_MS 450`. # Server-side melee lag compensation (`feature/lag-compensation`)

## Context

The #52 latency work made building/mining feel instant at high ping, and its CHANGELOG named combat "the next frontier". The remaining pain: the client renders remote mobs 125–450 ms in the past (adaptive interpolation), so a high-ping player clicks a mob dead under their crosshair and the server — raycasting against *current* positions — misses. Fix: the client stamps attack commands with the server-timeline instant it was rendering; the server rewinds **melee target selection** to that instant (bounded), while damage/knockback/kill-credit still apply to the live mob. PvE only (no PvP exists); arrows stay as-is (travel time means players lead — documented future work). Chosen by the user 2026-07-05 over mobile/touch, IndexedDB saves, and a content batch.

Unstamped commands, single-player, and every other command are byte-for-byte current behavior. `docs/protocol.md:124-127` explicitly anticipated this ("the envelope already carries what stricter server-side rewind validation would need").

## Verified ground truth

- Client sends bare `{type:"attack"}` + claimed foot pose (`lib/net/NetworkSession.ts:677-690`); room re-applies pose then `engine.dispatch(cmd, playerId)` (`server/room.ts:327-346`); `findAimedMobIndex` raycasts eye→look-dir against current `mob.position` within `ATTACK_REACH`/`ATTACK_AIM_DOT` (`lib/game/engine/systems/combat.ts:44-65`); `tryAttackMob` (75-101) damages + stamps `lastHitByPlayer`, knockback from live position.
- The render time on the server timeline is already computed each frame: `clock.estimatedServerTimeMs(nowMs) - delayCtl.effectiveDelayMs(nowMs)` (`NetworkSession.ts:805`) — not sent today.
- Room ticks 20 Hz with `tickCount`; tick msg carries tick number `n`; client maps n→ms via `n * 50` (`NetworkSession.ts:540`). No pose history exists; precedents: `mobShadow`, `commandLog` ring (room.ts).
- Mobs have stable numeric wire ids (`mob.id`); melee iterates only `state.mobs` → **players need no history**.
- `PROTOCOL_VERSION = 2` (`lib/net/protocol.ts:20`); bump refuses stale clients at handshake and via ticket `pv` claim (`server/index.ts:97-99`). Total-validation readers + well-formed/garbage test pattern in `protocol.test.ts`.
- No server melee cooldown (only the 60/s cmd flood guard, `room.ts:328`); clamp precedent `MAX_REMOTE_POSE_ELAPSED` (`GameEngine.ts:205,467`).

## Key decisions

- **View stamp = the previous frame's render time**, captured in `afterFrame` into a `lastRenderTimeMs` closure var — it's literally the time the on-screen poses were sampled with, and re-computing at click would double-advance the clock slew (`estimatedServerTimeMs` mutates slew state). `null` until the clock is ready → omit the field.
- **Selection-only rewind**: `posOf(mob)` resolver threaded into `findAimedMobIndex`; knockback/damage/kill-credit use the live mob. Mobs despawned since the viewed tick aren't in `state.mobs` — no resurrection by construction.
- **Bound**: `MELEE_REWIND_MAX_MS = 900` in `config.ts` (≈ interp max 450 + half-RTT budget + a tick) → 18 ticks; clamp `viewTick` into `[tickCount − 18, tickCount]`; future/garbage stamps degrade to live behavior.
- **Protocol v2→v3** per house policy (versioned as a whole; ticket `pv` makes rollout atomic). Deploy note: web + game server together; stale tabs get `CLOSE_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH` and refresh.
- **No engine melee cooldown** (would break SP/MP feel parity); instead a room-level per-second attack budget (12/s, beside the existing flood guard) to bound trail-sweeping abuse.
- **Precision note (document, don't fix)**: history is true 20 Hz; client renders deadbanded 10 Hz mob deltas; `view` rounds to the nearest tick — worst-case selection error ≈ 0.1 m against a 27° cone and 4.5 reach.

## Slices (branch `feature/lag-compensation` off main)

### Slice 1 — `feat(protocol): optional view stamp on cmd; bump protocol to v3`
`lib/net/protocol.ts` (+test): `CmdMessage.view?: number` (ms on the server tick timeline; absent when unsynced); total validation in the `"cmd"` case of `readClientMessage` (bad `view` → whole message null); `PROTOCOL_VERSION = 3`. Tests: round-trip with/without `view`; `"abc"`/`NaN`/`Infinity` rejected; `view` on non-attack cmds parses (semantics are the room's).

### Slice 2 — `feat(engine): thread a mob-position resolver into melee target selection`
`lib/game/engine/systems/combat.ts`: `export type MobPositionOf = (mob: MobState) => {x,y,z}`; `findAimedMobIndex(..., posOf = (mob) => mob.position)` uses `posOf` in its loop (`scratchToMob.set(p.x,p.y,p.z)`); `tryAttackMob(..., posOf?)` forwards to selection only — knockback block keeps live `mob.position`. Feed/tame callers unchanged via the default.
`GameEngine.ts`: `dispatch(command, playerId?, opts?: DispatchOptions)` with `DispatchOptions = { mobPosOf?: MobPositionOf }`, threaded to the attack case (~line 933). Doc on the type: server-only; the room is the sole producer; opts never cross `routeDispatch`.
Tests: `combat.test.ts` — historical-in-cone/live-behind mob hits, live hp drops, knockback sign derives from live position; `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` — `dispatch({type:"attack"}, "acct-2", {mobPosOf})`.

### Slice 3 — `feat(server): per-tick mob pose ring buffer`
New `server/mobHistory.ts` (+test): `createMobPoseHistory(depth = MOB_HISTORY_DEPTH /* 24 */)` → `{ record(tick, mobs), positionAt(tick, mobId) }`. Slot = `tick % depth`; parallel reused arrays (tick/count + id/x/y/z), no per-tick allocation once warm; `positionAt` → null on slot-tick mismatch or unknown id. Tests: round-trip, unknown id, wraparound eviction, slot re-record, never-recorded tick.

### Slice 4 — `feat(server): rewind melee target selection to the attacker's view tick`
`lib/game/config.ts`: `MELEE_REWIND_MAX_MS = 900` (combat block ~line 112). `server/room.ts`: `mobHistory` field; in `tick()` right after `engine.step(dt)`: `mobHistory.record(this.tickCount, engine.state.mobs)` (post-step = what this tick broadcasts = the client's buffer timeline). In the `"cmd"` case (after pose apply, before the dispatch at `room.ts:344`): if attack + `view` present → `viewTick = round(view/50)`, clamp into `[tickCount−18, tickCount]`, and if in the past pass `opts = { mobPosOf: (mob) => mobHistory.positionAt(rewindTick, mob.id) ?? mob.position }`. Add `view` to the cmd `CommandLogEntry`.
Tests (`room.test.ts`, fakeSink + manual `tick(0.05)`): (1) mob in front ticks 1–5, teleported 20 blocks away, attack at T+3 with `view: 4*50` hits / unstamped misses; (2) stale `view` beyond 18 ticks → miss; future `view` → live; (3) mob spawned after viewed tick → live fallback still hits; (4) existing no-view test untouched; (5) `view` on a non-attack cmd is inert.

### Slice 5 — `feat(server): per-second melee attack budget`
`server/room.ts`: `budget.attack`, reset with cmd/chat (~line 400); drop attacks past 12/s before dispatch. Constant beside the flood guard. Test: 13th attack in a second dropped; resets next second.

### Slice 6 — `feat(net): stamp attack cmds with the client's render time`
`lib/net/NetworkSession.ts`: capture `lastRenderTimeMs` in `afterFrame` (line ~805, only when `clock.ready()`); `sendCmd` adds `...(command.type === "attack" && lastRenderTimeMs !== null ? { view: Math.round(Math.max(0, lastRenderTimeMs)) } : {})`. No feel change (swing already instant via `routeDispatch`; echo swallow unchanged). Skip an F3 rewind readout (would need a server echo; `interpDelayMs` already tells the story).
Tests (`NetworkSession.test.ts`): stamped attack ≈ `n*50 − delay` after a pong+frame; no stamp before sync; non-attack cmds never stamped.
Note: slices 2–5 are inert in production until this slice — good bisectability.

### Slice 7 — `docs: melee lag compensation`
protocol.md (`view` field, v3 row, rewrite the trust-model "soft spot" bullet at ~124-127 to the shipped bound); architecture.md (combat + multiplayer-client sections); tuning.md (`MELEE_REWIND_MAX_MS`, history depth, attack budget); testing.md rows (+ note: deliberately no new e2e — latency scenarios stay in unit tests per policy); CHANGELOG (+ future work: arrow rewind intentionally skipped).

## Out of scope
Arrow/projectile rewind, PvP (doesn't exist), predicted hit effects, F3 rewind telemetry.

## Verification
- Per slice: `bun test <touched>` + `bun run format` + `bun run lint` (full gate is CI's job per local workflow; run the full gate once before the PR).
- Full gate pre-PR: lint, typecheck, format:check, `bun test`, build, `bun run test:e2e` (`multiplayer.e2e.ts` unchanged — proves v3 handshake + no regression under `setSimulatedLatency`; check port 3000 free first).
- Manual (two browsers, local server): attacker on `setSimulatedLatency(300, 50)` melees a walking mob under the crosshair — hits that previously whiffed register; at latency 0 and in SP, feel unchanged.
- PR deploy note: web app + game server deploy together (v3 tickets); Fly single-machine invariant unchanged.

## Risks
- `DispatchOptions` must never be expected to survive `routeDispatch` (documented at the type).
- Moving-mob room test could flake from mob AI drift — mitigate with `moveSpeed: 0` fixtures and 20-block separations; pin positions before each tick if needed.
- Synchronized deploy required (protocol bump) — same rollover as MP v2, known procedure.

## Reused existing code
`clock.estimatedServerTimeMs` + `DelayController.effectiveDelayMs` (`lib/net/clock.ts`, `lib/net/interpolation.ts`), the `applyRemotePose` clamp precedent (`GameEngine.ts:467`), `commandLog`/`budget` room patterns (`server/room.ts`), total-validation reader style (`lib/net/protocol.ts`), `room.test.ts` fakeSink/manual-tick harness, `combat.test.ts` `mobInFront` fixture.

# Mobile/touch play (`feature/touch-play`)

## Context

The PWA made Monecraft installable everywhere; lag comp fixed online combat feel — but the game is unplayable without a mouse. This adds touch play (virtual joystick, drag-look, action buttons) for tablets and landscape phones. Chosen by the user 2026-07-06 over IndexedDB saves and a content batch. **Merge gate: automated tests only** (user's call) — the real-device checklist is a documented post-merge fast-follow; feel constants live in `config.ts`/tuning.md precisely so device tuning needs no system changes.

The engine is already input-agnostic (verified): `FrameInput {move, mineHeld}` (`state.ts:442-455`) + `Command` dispatches + `engine.applyLook(dYaw,dPitch)` (`GameEngine.ts:1044`, pitch clamped there); ALL aiming is center-screen — zero cursor picking. Touch is an additive input layer, not a refactor. Zero touch/pointer/mobile code exists today; CSS is fixed-px with two width-only 720px breakpoints; `ItemTooltip` is hover-only; ~11 keyboard verbs need triage.

## Scope

**v1 (core play, tablets + landscape phones):** joystick move + PE-classic sprint (double-tap-forward-hold), drag-look, tap=attack / hold=mine on the look zone, buttons for Place/Jump/Sneak/Eat(contextual), top bar Pause/Inventory/Camera, hotbar tap-select (already works), inventory click-to-swap (already works) + an X close button, long-press tooltips, pause-menu touch toggle (auto/on/off) + Emergency Unstuck button, tap-to-play gate (no pointer lock), flight via double-tap Jump.
**Deferred (documented):** touch chat typing, F3, advancements button, keybinding customization, tap-a-block targeting, mobile perf knobs (DPR 1.5 cap / render-radius scaling), keyboard+touch hybrid simultaneity.

## Key decisions

- **Gesture model (PE-classic)**: tap on the free look area = one `attack`; press-and-hold within slop = `attack` + `mineHeld` until lift (mirrors desktop mousedown at `inputController.ts:168-172`); drift beyond slop = pure look drag, never mines. Mining stays on the look thumb so mine-while-aiming needs one finger; Place must be a button anyway (no right-click analog); Eat is a contextual button (`slot.hunger != null || slot.effect != null`), dispatching `eatFood`/`drinkPotion` per the KeyF rule (`inputController.ts:132-137`).
- **`engage()`/`release()` seam** (Slice 2, zero-behavior-change refactor): the `InputController` type gains these two methods; `useMinecraftGame`'s direct `pointerLockElement`/`exitPointerLock`/`requestPointerLock` pokes (verified at `useMinecraftGame.ts:354,368,444,451-453,524`) route through them. Touch then implements a **virtual lock**: `pointerLocked` reports an `active` flag, tap-to-play calls `engage()`, and the shell's `locked`-as-"is playing" plumbing (`MinecraftGame.tsx:140`, `ChatPanel.tsx:63`) works unchanged. `forcePointerLock` sets `active` silently → `e2e/helpers.ts` untouched.
- **Controller/overlay split**: `lib/game/input/touchInputController.ts` (DOM-free except `visibilitychange`→release+pause, the touch analog of lock-loss-pause; injectable now/schedule/cancel for deterministic tests) owns FrameInput mutation/applyLook/dispatch/gesture state machine; `components/game/TouchControls.tsx` is dumb rendering + Pointer Events forwarding `{pointerId,x,y}` (pointerType-agnostic so `page.mouse` drives it in e2e; `setPointerCapture` in try/catch). Overlay unmounts whenever a panel/death/pause is up; cleanup calls `clearKeys()`.
- **Mode**: `auto | on | off` in `lib/game/input/touchSettings.ts` (audio-settings pattern, key `minecraft_touch_v1`); auto = `(pointer: coarse)` && `maxTouchPoints > 0`; PauseMenu Options toggle; **hot-swap** via an `inputRef` + `swapController()` (fallback if the effect lifecycle fights back: apply on next world entry — decide in-branch, note in PR).
- **Constants** (config.ts, tuning.md "Touch feel" section): `TOUCH_LOOK_SENSITIVITY 0.0042` (2× mouse — thumb travel is short), `TOUCH_TAP_MAX_MS 220`, `TOUCH_TAP_SLOP_PX 12`, `TOUCH_HOLD_MINE_MS 220` (= TAP_MAX, no ambiguity gap), `TOUCH_JOYSTICK_RADIUS_PX 64`, `TOUCH_JOYSTICK_DEADZONE 0.18`, `TOUCH_SPRINT_DOUBLE_TAP_MS 300`, `TOUCH_LONGPRESS_TOOLTIP_MS 450`. Joystick: 8-way sectors via `DIAG = sin(π/8)` on the normalized vector; deadzone zeroes intents. Flight double-tap reuses `FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS`.
- **iOS realities** (Slice 4): `userScalable:false` alone does NOT stop double-tap zoom — global `touch-action: manipulation` + `none` on game surfaces is the real fix (NOT on `.game-root` — effective touch-action intersects ancestors and would kill panel scrolling); `-webkit-touch-callout: none`; `100dvh` as an override line after `100vh` (iOS 15.4+ with fallback); safe-areas need `viewportFit: "cover"` + `env(safe-area-inset-*)` vars; `interactiveWidget: "resizes-content"` (anvil rename input opens a keyboard).
- **Desktop stays pixel- and behavior-identical**: height-based media queries only add below 480px height; Slice 2 is refactor-only; the full existing e2e suite is the desktop regression guard.

## Slices (branch `feature/touch-play` off main)

1. **`feat(input): touch settings with auto device detection`** — `touchSettings.ts` (+test): read/write/validate (injectable storage + window-shaped `{matchMedia, navigator}`), `resolveTouchEnabled(mode)`.
2. **`refactor(input): engage/release seam on InputController`** — extend the type + desktop impl (`engage` = current :451-453 body; `release` = exit-if-canvas-holds-lock); reroute `useMinecraftGame` :354/:368/:444/:524; introduce `inputRef` (rAF reads `inputRef.current.input` at :340). Zero behavior change; desktop e2e green is the gate.
3. **`feat(input): touch input controller`** — `touchInputController.ts` (+test, stub engine + fake clock): joystick math, sprint latch, look/tap/hold/cancel state machine, jump double-tap flight, gates (`active` && !`uiBlocked`), visibilitychange→release+pause, clearKeys/dispose. Constants into config.ts + tuning.md.
4. **`feat(ui): mobile viewport, safe areas, and short-landscape layout`** — layout.tsx viewport fields; base/hud/ui/menu.css: touch-action, callout/user-select, dvh overrides, safe-area vars + hud-bottom/minimap insets, extend the 720px blocks to `(max-width:720px), (max-height:480px)` + a short-landscape panel-padding block.
5. **`feat(ui): touch controls overlay wired into the game shell`** — `TouchControls.tsx` (+test with mock api), `app/touch.css`; `useMinecraftGame`: settings load, controller pick, `touch` + `engageControls` exposure, `pointerdown` added to audio-unlock listeners (:314-316); `MinecraftGame.tsx`: overlay under the suppression condition, "Tap to play" hint variant with full-area engage, hide caps-indicator on touch; `InventoryPanel` gains an optional X close (desktop too; +test).
6. **`feat(ui): touch mode toggle + unstuck button in the pause menu`** — Options segmented Auto/On/Off; Game tab Emergency Unstuck (`unstuck` + resume — helps desktop too); Controls tab touch gesture rows; hook `updateTouchSettings` + `swapController`. (+PauseMenu tests)
7. **`feat(ui): long-press item tooltips on touch`** — extend `useItemTooltip().bind()`: pointerdown (non-mouse) starts a 450 ms timer → show anchored; move>slop/up/cancel cancels; `onClickCapture` suppresses the post-long-press click (recipe entries use `is-disabled`, they DO fire clicks); document pointerdown dismisses. Mouse path byte-identical. (+tests)
8. **`test(e2e): touch play smoke`** — helpers gain a `touchMode` option fixture seeding `minecraft_touch_v1` (Playwright `hasTouch` doesn't flip `pointer: coarse` — forced mode sidesteps detection, which Slice 1 unit-covers); `e2e/touch.e2e.ts` with `test.use({ touchMode:"on", hasTouch:true, viewport:{812×375} })`: tap-to-play → virtual lock; joystick moves the player; drag changes yaw; hold sets `mineHeld` (real block break if stable); Place consumes an item; Pause→resume exercises touch `engage()`; Options toggle proves the hot-swap (`__monecraft.input` identity change). Desktop suite must stay green.
9. **`docs: touch play`** — README (revise `:19` "Not a mobile game…" + Touch controls subsection), manual.md controls, architecture.md input section (two controllers, one type, virtual-lock story, warning: never read `pointerLockElement` directly — use the seam), testing.md rows, CHANGELOG, AGENTS.md manual-pass rule (+ touch-control changes) + the device checklist location.

## Edge cases
Rotation: joystick origin computed per pointerdown; `orientationchange` → `renderer.handleResize()` + `clearKeys()` (register in the hook, harmless on desktop). Death/station events already `clearKeys()` (:353/:362); overlay unmount repeats it (idempotent). `pointercancel` everywhere = lift-without-action. Touch pause = `release()` then `dispatch pause` — no double-pause (auto-pause-on-lock-loss is desktop-only). Hybrid keyboard+touch: touch mode replaces keyboard in v1 (documented; `off` restores).

## Verification
- Per slice: `bun run format` + `lint` (per-commit gate); full gate (typecheck, format:check, bun test, build) + full `test:e2e` before the PR (port 3000 lsof check first).
- **Merge gate = automated only** (user decision 2026-07-06). The 16-item real-device checklist (iPhone Safari landscape, iPad, Android Chrome: detection, audio unlock, 3-contact concurrency, gesture discrimination, safe-areas, no zoom/callout, rotation, app-switch, PWA install, perf spot-check) ships in the PR description as the named fast-follow; feel-constant tuning lands as a config-only follow-up commit.
- Known risk ranking: mobile GPU perf (measure on device; DPR/radius knobs are named future work) > hot-swap-in-effect (fallback: apply on re-entry) > `locked` drift (architecture.md warning) > feel constants (config-only tuning).

## Reused existing code
`InputController` type + factory pattern (`lib/game/input/inputController.ts`), `FrameInput`/`applyLook`/Command seams (engine untouched), audio-settings persistence pattern (`lib/game/audio/settings.ts`), `useItemTooltip` (extended, not replaced), `.game-root` z-layer + pointer-events conventions, seeded-world e2e fixture (`e2e/helpers.ts`), `FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS`.

feat(input): touch input controller

The heart of touch play: a DOM-free gesture state machine implementing
the same InputController surface as the desktop controller, with
gameplay capture as a virtual `active` flag behind engage()/release()
(there is no pointer lock to acquire on touch — tap-to-play flips it).

Gesture model is Minecraft-PE classic: on the free look area, drag =
look (deltas through engine.applyLook from the first move), a quick
still tap = one attack, and a press held within slop = attack +
mineHeld until lift — while a drag that leaves the slop first can only
ever be a look, so a camera swipe never digs. The joystick maps to
8-way move intents with a deadzone; re-engaging it inside 300 ms
latches sprint, applied only while pushing forward. Jump double-tap
toggles flight (mirroring Space); Sneak is a latching toggle (holding a
corner button while juggling two thumbs is a hand-cramp); Eat picks
eatFood vs drinkPotion by the held slot, the KeyF rule.

Time and scheduling are injectable, so every tap/hold/sprint window is
unit-tested against a fake clock. visibilitychange while active
releases and pauses — the touch analog of losing pointer lock. Feel
constants live in config.ts (documented trade-offs in tuning.md) so the
pending real-device pass tunes them without touching systems.
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -1

feat(ui): touch controls overlay wired into the game shell

The visible half of touch play. TouchControls is deliberately dumb —
a full-screen look pad at z3 (above the canvas, below the HUD, so
hotbar taps still hit the hotbar and everything that falls through
becomes look/mine input), a fixed-base joystick with a clamped visual
knob, an action cluster (Jump/Sneak/Place + a contextual Eat that
appears when the held slot is consumable), and a top bar
(pause/inventory/camera). It only converts PointerEvents into
{pointerId, x, y} records; every gesture decision stays in the
unit-tested controller. Handlers are pointerType-agnostic so a mouse
drives the overlay too (dev + Playwright).

The hook picks the controller per world boot from the persisted touch
mode, exposes the controls api plus pauseNow/toggleInventory (which
mirror the desktop key paths: clear keys + release capture before the
panel), covers resize/orientationchange for the DOM-free touch
controller, and adds pointerdown to the audio-unlock listeners —
touch-action: none can suppress the synthetic mousedown the desktop
unlock path relies on. The click hint becomes a full-screen "Tap to
play" surface on touch; the CapsLock indicator hides (sprint lives on
the joystick). InventoryPanel gains an X close button — touch has no
KeyI/Escape, and it helps desktop too.
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -1

content.content:
- `footsteps.ts` / `mobAmbience.ts` / `musicBrain.ts` — pure schedulers/composer (distance-accumulator strides, per-mob randomized call timers with distance gain + look-relative stereo pan, pentatonic random-walk note generation). `musicPlayer.ts` renders notes as detuned pad voices through a lowpass and a procedural convolution reverb.
- **Lazy unlock invariant**: no `AudioContext` exists until the first user gesture calls `unlock()` — including the `zzfx` import itself, which instantiates one at module scope and is therefore only ever imported dynamically inside `unlock()`. This satisfies the browser autoplay policy, keeps SSR/`bun test` import-safe, and keeps the console clean for the E2E fixture.
- Volume settings (`settings.ts`) persist under their own localStorage key (`minecraft_audio_v1`) — never part of the world save.

## Input (`lib/game/input/inputController.ts`)

Owns every DOM listener **and the DOM→intent mapping**: raw key codes, CapsLock, and pointer lock never leave this module. Continuous input is reduced to the abstract `FrameInput` (`move.{forward,back,left,right,jump,sprint,crouch}` + `mineHeld`) the engine reads each step — the engine has no notion of key bindings or the cursor (`mineHeld` already folds in "left mouse held **and** pointer locked"), which is what lets any input source (keyboard, future gamepad/keybinding screen, a network client's intent packets, replays) drive the same simulation. Discrete actions (hotbar, inventory toggle, place, eat, attack, unstuck, pause, F3 debug, V camera view) become commands; mouse-look calls `engine.applyLook`. The first click only acquires pointer lock; `KeyI` exits it. Tests build inputs via `frameInput` (`lib/game/engine/testSupport.ts`), which still speaks key-code names ("hold KeyW") but emits intents; the E2E pointer-lock fallback uses the controller's `forcePointerLock` test hook.

**Pause ↔ pointer lock**: the browser consumes Escape to exit pointer lock, so Esc never reaches keydown while locked — losing the lock during plain gameplay is the pause trigger (`pointerlockchange` dispatches `pause`). The inventory (`KeyI`) and death paths set their state flags _before_ the async `pointerlockchange` fires, and the engine's `pause` command additionally ignores those states, so they don't open the menu. While unlocked, Escape toggles pause directly (and closes the inventory). "Back to Game" resumes and re-requests the lock; Chrome's ~1.25 s cooldown after Esc can reject that request — the rejection is swallowed and the player just clicks the canvas.

## Multiplayer client (`lib/net/`)

Online play mounts the **same** shell/renderer/audio/input stack on a different engine: `connectNetworkSession(url, ticket)` (`NetworkSession.ts`) performs the hello → welcome → gzipped world-sync handshake, then constructs a **replica** engine (`replica: true, bootPlayer: false` — worldgen from the server's seed is byte-identical thanks to `lib/world/noise.ts`, the world sync applies the block diff/containers/mobs on top). `useMinecraftGame` accepts the session via its `online` option: the replica engine is mounted instead of constructing one, localStorage persistence is skipped (the server owns the world), replicated server events join the local event drain (so toasts/audio/particles treat them like local ones), and `session.afterFrame` runs each rAF.

   sword** (2 cobble + 1 wood) — both upgrades over your starting wood pickaxe and
   knife.
3. **Mine and gather.** Hold **left-click** to break trees, stone, and dirt for

| `C`                | Crouch (slower, careful movement)                                                                             |

# Monecraft (Next.js + TypeScript + Three.js + Bun)

[![CI](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/hutusi/monecraft?label=release&sort=semver)](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/tags)

A playable, Minecraft-inspired voxel game that runs entirely in your browser. Explore procedural terrain across five biomes, cross water by **raft** or **ship** — over living oceans with **fish**, **kelp**, sunken **shipwrecks** to dive, and **buried treasure** to hunt by map — and dig into **dark caves** — lit only by the torches you craft and place, where lava pools and mobs lurk. Mine ores, raid **underground dungeons** for loot, build and farm, breed animals, craft through seven gear tiers up to a **bow** and throwable **spears**, and take on an **endgame boss** for a true win condition — all across a day-night cycle with hunger, drowning, and lava hazards.

The twist: **everything is procedural — zero binary assets.** Block textures and item sprites are painted from pixel code, all sound and music is synthesized at runtime, and lighting is computed per voxel. Single-player is client-only: keep **multiple worlds** under **multiple player profiles**, all saved to localStorage, no account needed. Or play **online co-op** (2–8 players): host a server-backed world with a free account and share an invite link — friends register and join in a click. See [docs/manual.md](docs/manual.md#playing-online).

## Run

```bash
bun install
bun run dev
```

Then open `http://localhost:3000`.

Monecraft is also an installable **PWA**: in a Chromium browser, the address-bar install button turns it into a desktop app, and after the first visit **single-player works fully offline** (online features — accounts, cloud saves, co-op — still need a connection). Not a mobile game: it needs a mouse and pointer lock.

The game opens with a choice: **Sign in** for online play (co-op worlds, cloud saves — a free account), or **Play locally** with browser profiles and no account. Locally, pick or create a **profile** (your name and look), then create or choose a **world** to play. New worlds let you pick a **type** — Default, Superflat, Amplified, or Islands — a **game mode**, a **difficulty** (Peaceful · Easy · Normal · Hard), an optional **Hardcore** toggle (permadeath, locked to Survival + Hard), and a seed. Each profile keeps its own list of worlds, so several players can share one browser. Inside the game, **Esc → Save & Quit to Worlds** returns to the world list.

## Controls

- `W A S D`: Move · `Space`: Jump · `C`: Crouch
- `W + CapsLock`: Sprint (drains hunger)
- Double-tap `Space`: Toggle flight in Creative (Spectator always flies); then `Space` / `C` to rise / descend
- `Mouse`: Look around (double-click the game first to lock the pointer)
- `Left click` (hold): Break block / attack mobs
- `Right click` or `E`: Place/interact, board rafts, place water vehicles, or throw a selected spear
- `1..9`: Select hotbar slot
- `I`: Inventory & crafting · `L`: Advancements & statistics · `F`: Eat food · `Shift+U`: Emergency unstuck
- `V`: Camera view (first-person → third-person rear → third-person front)
- `T` or `Enter`: Chat (online worlds)
- `Esc`: Pause menu — three tabs: **Game** (save / load / reset, **Save & Quit to Worlds**, the **Game Mode** and **Difficulty** switchers), **Options** (sound/music volume, Appearance skins), and **Controls** · `F3`: Debug overlay

New here? The [player manual](docs/manual.md) walks through your first day, survival, crafting, farming, mobs, and more.

## Development

```bash
bun run lint        # ESLint
bun run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
bun test            # unit + integration + component tests
bun run build       # production build
bun run test:e2e    # Playwright browser smoke tests
bun run format      # Prettier
```

All of these are enforced by CI on every PR. The game simulation is a headless engine (no DOM), so gameplay logic is covered by real simulation tests, and a Playwright smoke suite exercises the browser layers — see [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md).

## Docs

- [docs/manual.md](docs/manual.md) — player guide: getting started, survival, crafting, mobs, farming
- [docs/reference.md](docs/reference.md) — scannable tables: recipes, blocks, mobs, and item stats
- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) — engine/renderer/shell layering and invariants
- [docs/adding-content.md](docs/adding-content.md) — add a block, item, recipe, mob, or mechanic
- [docs/save-format.md](docs/save-format.md) — save schema and compatibility rules
- [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md) — deploy online multiplayer (Vercel + Neon + Fly.io)
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — workflow and verification baseline

## Input (`lib/game/input/inputController.ts`)

Owns every DOM listener **and the DOM→intent mapping**: raw key codes, CapsLock, and pointer lock never leave this module. Continuous input is reduced to the abstract `FrameInput` (`move.{forward,back,left,right,jump,sprint,crouch}` + `mineHeld`) the engine reads each step — the engine has no notion of key bindings or the cursor (`mineHeld` already folds in "left mouse held **and** pointer locked"), which is what lets any input source (keyboard, future gamepad/keybinding screen, a network client's intent packets, replays) drive the same simulation. Discrete actions (hotbar, inventory toggle, place, eat, attack, unstuck, pause, F3 debug, V camera view) become commands; mouse-look calls `engine.applyLook`. The first click only acquires pointer lock; `KeyI` exits it. Tests build inputs via `frameInput` (`lib/game/engine/testSupport.ts`), which still speaks key-code names ("hold KeyW") but emits intents; the E2E pointer-lock fallback uses the controller's `forcePointerLock` test hook.

**Pause ↔ pointer lock**: the browser consumes Escape to exit pointer lock, so Esc never reaches keydown while locked — losing the lock during plain gameplay is the pause trigger (`pointerlockchange` dispatches `pause`). The inventory (`KeyI`) and death paths set their state flags _before_ the async `pointerlockchange` fires, and the engine's `pause` command additionally ignores those states, so they don't open the menu. While unlocked, Escape toggles pause directly (and closes the inventory). "Back to Game" resumes and re-requests the lock; Chrome's ~1.25 s cooldown after Esc can reject that request — the rejection is swallowed and the player just clicks the canvas.

## Input (`lib/game/input/`)

**Two controllers, one type.** `createInputController` (mouse/keyboard + pointer lock) and `createTouchInputController` (virtual joystick / drag-look / on-screen buttons) both implement the same `InputController` surface, and `useMinecraftGame` picks one per world boot from the persisted touch mode (`touchSettings.ts`: `auto` = coarse-pointer && touch points, with explicit on/off overrides; the pause-menu toggle hot-swaps the live controller through the shell's `inputRef` without tearing down the renderer). Each owns its own DOM listeners and DOM→intent mapping: raw key codes, CapsLock, pointer lock, and pointer gestures never leave this directory. Continuous input is reduced to the abstract `FrameInput` (`move.{forward,back,left,right,jump,sprint,crouch}` + `mineHeld`) the engine reads each step — the engine has no notion of key bindings or the cursor (`mineHeld` already folds in "held **and** gameplay captured"), which is what lets any input source (keyboard, touch, future gamepad, a network client's intent packets, replays) drive the same simulation. Discrete actions (hotbar, inventory toggle, place, eat, attack, unstuck, pause, F3 debug, V camera view) become commands; look calls `engine.applyLook`.

**The engage/release seam (invariant).** "Enter/leave gameplay capture" goes through `InputController.engage()`/`release()` — desktop maps them to request/exit pointer lock, touch flips a **virtual** `active` flag (there is no pointer lock on touch; tap-to-play calls `engage()` and `pointerLocked` reports the flag so the shell's `locked` plumbing works unchanged). **Never call `requestPointerLock`/`exitPointerLock` or read `pointerLockElement` from shell code directly** — it would silently desync the touch controller. Tests build inputs via `frameInput` (`lib/game/engine/testSupport.ts`); the E2E pointer-lock fallback uses `forcePointerLock`, which both controllers implement (flip the engine-facing gate without telling the React shell).

**Touch gestures** (`touchInputController.ts`, DOM-free — the `TouchControls` overlay forwards plain pointer records, so the state machine unit-tests without a browser): on the free look area, drag = look, tap = one `attack`, press-and-hold within the tap slop = `attack` + `mineHeld` until lift — a drag that leaves the slop first can only ever be a look. The joystick maps to 8-way move intents; quick re-engage latches sprint (applied only while pushing forward); Jump double-tap toggles flight; Sneak is a latching toggle. Feel constants live in `config.ts` (see tuning.md "Touch feel"). `visibilitychange` while active releases and pauses — the touch analog of pointer-lock loss. Hover-only item tooltips gain a long-press path on touch (`ItemTooltip.tsx`); the post-long-press click is swallowed so it never doubles as a slot click.

**Pause ↔ pointer lock (desktop)**: the browser consumes Escape to exit pointer lock, so Esc never reaches keydown while locked — losing the lock during plain gameplay is the pause trigger (`pointerlockchange` dispatches `pause`). The inventory (`KeyI`) and death paths set their state flags _before_ the async `pointerlockchange` fires, and the engine's `pause` command additionally ignores those states, so they don't open the menu. While unlocked, Escape toggles pause directly (and closes the inventory). "Back to Game" resumes and calls `engage()`; Chrome's ~1.25 s cooldown after Esc can reject the lock request — the rejection is swallowed and the player just clicks the canvas. On touch, the pause button calls `release()` **then** dispatches `pause` explicitly (no auto-pause is chained to a virtual release).

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, …) working in this repository. This file is the single source of truth — CLAUDE.md imports it.

## Project

A Minecraft-inspired voxel game: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), React 19, TypeScript (strict), Three.js, Bun. Single-player, browser-based, client-only, saves to localStorage.

**Zero binary assets**: every asset is generated at runtime — textures and sprites from pixel code, sound and music synthesized via ZZFX/WebAudio. New content should follow this principle unless the user decides otherwise. The one sanctioned exception is the UI pixel font (Monocraft, a Minecraft-style face under the SIL OFL 1.1), self-hosted via `next/font/local` from the committed woff2 in `app/fonts/` — don't "fix" it back to a system font. `public/` holds only code (the service worker `sw.js`) — no images or media belong there.

## Commands

```bash
bun install        # Install dependencies
bun run dev        # Dev server at http://localhost:3000
bun run build      # Production build — part of the verification baseline
bun run lint       # ESLint (flat config, eslint .)
bun run typecheck  # next typegen + tsc --noEmit
bun run format     # Prettier --write (CI runs format:check — unformatted files fail the build)
bun test           # Unit + integration + component tests
bun run test:e2e   # Playwright browser smoke tests (needs `bunx playwright install chromium` once)
```

## Development Workflow

For a non-trivial change:

- **Branch only for big work.** A new feature, a large refactor or improvement, a dependency upgrade, or broad/risky work spanning many systems gets its own `<type>/<topic>` branch off `main` (e.g. `upgrade/next16-react19-three184`) so it lands as one reviewable unit. Minor work — bug fixes, small improvements, doc edits, single-purpose tweaks — commits straight to `main`, even when it touches a few files. ### Added

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	### Added
8	
9	- **Melee lag compensation — clicking the mob you SEE now hits it at any ping (protocol v2→v3)**: in an online world your screen renders mobs 125–450 ms in the past (the interpolation delay), so at high ping a melee swing aimed dead at a mob used to whiff — the server judged it against positions your screen hadn't shown yet. Attacks now carry the instant of the world you were looking at (the frame's render time on the server clock), and the server rewinds **target selection** to that instant against its own recorded mob history, bounded to 900 ms (`MELEE_REWIND_MAX_MS`) — damage, knockback, and kill credit still land on the live mob, so nothing resurrects and no consequence time-travels. Anything degenerate (an unsynced clock, a stale or future stamp, a mob spawned since the viewed tick) simply judges live, exactly as before; single-player is untouched. A 12-attacks/second server budget keeps the rewind window from being trawled by scripted spam. The protocol bump means the web app and game server deploy together; a stale tab is refused cleanly at the door. Bow arrows keep current behavior on purpose — travel time means players already lead their shots; rewinding swept projectile paths is heavier machinery for less felt benefit (future work).
10	- **Offline play (PWA, part 2)**: after one online visit, single-player boots with no connection — a hand-rolled service worker (`public/sw.js`, no workbox/serwist dependency) precaches the app shell and its static chunks, serves navigations network-first (deploys land normally and apply silently on the next online load), and **never touches** `/api/*`, the game-server connection, or invite links, so accounts, cloud saves, and multiplayer behave exactly as before. In development the registration component instead unregisters workers and clears caches, keeping `bun run dev` immune to a stale prod worker on the same origin. Pinned by classifier unit tests (`tests/sw.test.ts`) and an offline e2e (`e2e/pwa.e2e.ts`) that cuts the network and boots a world from the worker's cache.

2	
3	Two runners, three layers:
4	
5	- **`bun test`** — unit, integration, and component tests, colocated as `*.test.ts[x]` next to the code they cover (one exception: the service worker's tests live in `tests/sw.test.ts` — `public/` is deployed verbatim, so no test files belong there). 1	# Player Manual
2	
3	A complete guide to playing Monecraft — a single-player, browser-based voxel
4	sandbox. Mine, build, craft, farm, fight off the night, and survive.
5	
6	This page is the prose guide; for the exact numbers (every recipe, block, mob, and
7	item stat) see the [reference tables](reference.md). Just want the keys? They're in
8	the [README](../README.md#controls).
9	
10	> Everything you see and hear is generated from code at runtime — there are no
11	> image or audio files anywhere in the game.
12	
13	## Worlds & profiles
14	
15	The game opens to a menu rather than dropping you straight into a world:
16	
17	1. **Choose how to play.** The game opens with two doors: **Sign in** (online
18	   worlds and cloud saves — needs a free account, see
19	   [Playing online](#playing-online)) or **Play locally** (everything below —
20	   stored in this browser, no account).
21	2. **Pick a profile.** A profile is a player — a name and an appearance (skin). On a
22	   shared browser everyone can have their own. Create one with **New Profile**, choose
23	   a skin, and you're in; rename or delete profiles from the same screen.
24	3. **Pick a world.** Each profile keeps its **own** list of worlds. **New World** lets
25	   you name it, choose a **world type** (Default, Superflat, Amplified, or Islands —
26	   see [the reference](reference.md#world-types)), and optionally enter a **seed** —
27	   type a number or a word to get the same world every time, or leave it blank for a
28	   random one. Worlds you've played show most-recent first; rename or delete them here too.
29	4. **Play.** Choosing a world drops you in. From the pause menu (**Esc**), **Save &
30	   Quit to Worlds** takes you back to the list, and reloading the page resumes the
31	   world you were in.
32	
33	Everything is saved in your browser (localStorage). Deleting a world removes its save;
34	deleting a profile removes all of its worlds.
35	
36	## Getting started: your first day
37	
38	You spawn at dawn on solid ground with a small starter kit: stacks of grass, dirt,
39	stone, wood, planks, cobble, and sand, plus a **wood pickaxe** and a **knife**.
40	
41	The day-night cycle is short — **four minutes per full day** — so the first night
42	comes fast. A good opening:
43	
44	1. **Look around.** Double-click the game to lock the mouse (the starting gesture
45	   doesn't mine). Move with `W A S D`, look with the mouse. On a touch device,
46	   tap to play instead — move with the left joystick and drag the world to look.
47	2. **Gear up from your kit.** Open the inventory with **`I`**. You already have
48	   cobble and wood, so craft a **stone pickaxe** (2 cobble + 1 wood) and a **stone
49	   sword** (2 cobble + 1 wood) — both upgrades over your starting wood pickaxe and
50	   knife.
51	3. **Mine and gather.** Hold **left-click** to break trees, stone, and dirt for
52	   more materials; craft **2 wood → 4 planks** whenever you need them.
53	4. **Shelter before dark.** Wall yourself in with blocks (**right-click** or `E`
54	   to place the selected hotbar item), or craft a **bed** and skip the night
55	   entirely. Hostile mobs spawn once it gets dark, so don't be caught in the open.
56

Done — touch play is fully built and verified on `feature/touch-play` (9 commits, not pushed).

**What shipped, slice by slice:**

1. `4a59e66` **Touch settings** — persisted auto/on/off mode; auto requires *both* a coarse primary pointer and touch points (either alone misfires on TVs and touchscreen laptops).
2. `8a0ad7c` **The engage/release seam** — the zero-behavior-change refactor that makes everything else possible: the shell now enters/leaves "gameplay capture" through the controller instead of poking pointer-lock APIs directly, and the rAF loop reads through a ref so controllers can hot-swap.
3. `6970248` **The touch controller** — a DOM-free gesture state machine (PE-classic: tap=attack, hold=mine, drag=look with a hard slop boundary so a camera swipe never digs; joystick with double-engage sprint; jump double-tap flight), 19 unit tests against a fake clock.
4. `bfcf76d` **Mobile CSS groundwork** — safe-area vars, dvh fallback chains, `touch-action` done the way iOS actually honors it, and height-based breakpoints (landscape phones never triggered the old width-only ones). Desktop pixel-identical.
5. `e2815f9` **The overlay** — dumb PointerEvent routing (so `page.mouse` can drive it), joystick + action buttons + top bar, "Tap to play" gate, contextual Eat button, InventoryPanel X close.
6. `eeaa856` **Pause-menu toggle + Emergency Unstuck** — the Auto/On/Off override hot-swaps the controller mid-world without tearing down the renderer.
7. `a1ee765` **Long-press tooltips** — the recipe book's entire help system (missing ingredients, durability) was hover-only; now a 450 ms hold shows it, with the follow-up click swallowed exactly once.
8. `2ae2711` **Touch e2e** — 7 tests on a 812×375 `hasTouch` viewport; two real gotchas found and fixed in-branch (first-seconds mesh jank swallows synthetic pointer moves → settle convention; the lock flag flips before React commits the overlay → wait for the DOM).
9. `31ff12f` **Docs** — README loses "Not a mobile game", manual gains the gesture reference, architecture documents the never-poke-pointer-lock invariant, testing.md hosts the real-device checklist.

**Gate:** typecheck, format, lint, 1257 unit tests, build, and **31/31 e2e** (all 24 existing suites — the desktop-regression proof — plus 7 touch). No protocol, save-format, or worldgen impact.

**Per your merge-on-e2e decision:** the real-device pass (iPhone/iPad/Android — three-contact concurrency, feel-constant tuning, zoom/callout suppression, safe areas, framerate) is the named fast-follow, checklist in `docs/testing.md`; the `TOUCH_*` constants live in `config.ts` so tuning is config-only.
