gh pr create --repo hutusi/monecraft --base main --head feature/touch-play --title "feat: touch play — the installed PWA becomes playable on tablets and phones" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

The PWA made Monecraft installable everywhere; this makes it playable without a mouse. Tablets and landscape phones get on-screen controls automatically: a virtual joystick, drag-to-look, tap-to-attack / hold-to-mine, action buttons, long-press tooltips, and an Auto/On/Off override in the pause menu that hot-swaps the input method mid-world. Desktop play is byte-identical — the entire existing e2e suite is the regression proof.

**Merge gate (agreed): automated tests only.** The real-device pass is the named fast-follow — checklist in `docs/testing.md` ("Touch: the real-device checklist"); the feel constants (`TOUCH_*` in `config.ts`, documented trade-offs in tuning.md "Touch feel") shipped as educated guesses precisely so on-device tuning is a config-only follow-up.

## How it's built (one commit per slice)

1. **Touch settings**: persisted `auto | on | off`; auto flips only when a coarse primary pointer AND `maxTouchPoints > 0` agree — either alone misfires (coarse TVs without touch, touchscreen laptops with a mouse primary).
2. **The engage/release seam** (zero-behavior-change refactor): the shell previously poked `requestPointerLock`/`exitPointerLock`/`pointerLockElement` directly in four places; it now goes through `InputController.engage()/release()`, and the rAF loop reads the controller through a ref. This is what lets a touch controller exist at all — its "lock" is a **virtual** active flag (tap-to-play engages; `pointerLocked` reports it so the shell's `locked` plumbing works unchanged) — and what makes the mid-world hot-swap possible. The invariant is documented in architecture.md: shell code must never touch pointer-lock APIs directly again.
3. **The gesture state machine** (`touchInputController.ts`, DOM-free, injectable clock, 19 unit tests): PE-classic combat — tap = one attack, press-and-hold within a 12 px slop = attack + `mineHeld` until lift, and a drag that leaves the slop first can only ever be a look (a camera swipe never digs). Joystick → 8-way move intents with a deadzone; quick re-engage latches sprint (forward-only); Jump double-tap toggles flight; Sneak latches (holding a corner button while juggling two thumbs is a hand-cramp); Eat picks `eatFood` vs `drinkPotion` by the held slot (the KeyF rule). `visibilitychange` while active releases and pauses — the touch analog of pointer-lock loss.
4. **Mobile CSS groundwork**, desktop-invisible by construction: safe-area inset vars (needs the new `viewportFit: "cover"`), `100dvh` overrides behind `100vh` fallbacks, `touch-action: manipulation` globally + `none` on game surfaces (iOS ignores the zoom meta — and NOT on `.game-root`, where the ancestor intersection would kill panel scrolling), and the responsive breakpoints now fire on EITHER axis — a landscape phone (812×375) never triggered the old width-only queries.
5. **The overlay** (`TouchControls.tsx`): deliberately dumb — a look pad at z3 (hotbar taps still hit the hotbar; everything that falls through becomes look/mine), joystick with a clamped visual knob, action cluster, top bar. Handlers are pointerType-agnostic so a mouse (and Playwright) drives it. Plus: "Tap to play" hint variant, contextual Eat button, InventoryPanel X close (helps desktop too), `pointerdown` added to the audio-unlock listeners.
6. **Pause menu**: Touch Controls Auto/On/Off (hot-swap, falling back to the play gate — the honest UX for an input-method change) and **Emergency Unstuck** on the Game tab (Shift+U's only home for keyboardless players); the Controls tab shows gestures while touch is active.
7. **Long-press tooltips**: the tooltip system was hover-only, which on touch silently discarded the game's densest info surface (durability, the recipe book's missing-ingredient + how-to-obtain hints). `useItemTooltip().bind()` now also implements a 450 ms long-press with the follow-up click swallowed exactly once — every current and future tooltip surface gets it for free; the mouse path is byte-identical.
8. **Touch e2e** (7 tests, 812×375 `hasTouch`): tap-to-play, joystick walk, drag-look, hold-mine, button-place, pause round-trip, and the Options hot-swap (controller identity change, overlay unmount, desktop hint return — and back). The `gamePage` fixture gains a `touchMode` option seeding the forced-on preference: Playwright's `hasTouch` doesn't flip `(pointer: coarse)`, so detection is unit-tested instead.
9. **Docs**: README (the "Not a mobile game" sentence is gone; touch controls section), manual, architecture, testing (+ the device checklist), tuning, AGENTS.md (manual-pass rule now includes touch-control changes), CHANGELOG.

## Deferred (documented)

Touch chat typing (online co-op is joinable; typing UX later), F3 overlay, tap-a-block targeting (aiming stays center-crosshair, as in Minecraft PE classic), keybinding customization, mobile perf knobs (DPR 1.5 cap / render-radius scaling — the device pass will say whether they're needed).

## Verification

- Full gate green: `lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `bun test` (1257 pass, exit 0), `build`, full `test:e2e` — **31 passed** (all 24 existing suites + 7 touch).
- No protocol, save-format, or worldgen impact.
- Two e2e gotchas found and fixed in-branch, documented in the spec: first-seconds chunk-meshing jank can swallow synthetic pointer moves (tests follow the suite's settle convention), and the lock flag flips before React commits the overlay (tests wait for the DOM).
EOF

**Branch `feature/touch-play` complete locally (2026-07-06), 9 commits, tip `31ff12f`.** The installed PWA becomes playable on tablets/landscape phones: virtual joystick (8-way + double-engage sprint), drag-look, tap=attack/hold=mine (PE-classic, slop-bounded), Place/Jump/Sneak/Eat buttons, long-press tooltips, pause-menu Auto/On/Off toggle with mid-world hot-swap, Emergency Unstuck button, safe-area/dvh/short-landscape CSS. Architecture: `engage()/release()` seam on InputController (shell must NEVER poke pointer-lock APIs directly — documented invariant in architecture.md); touch controller is DOM-free with injectable clock (19 unit tests); overlay is dumb PointerEvent routing. Full gate green: 1257 unit / build / **31 e2e** (24 existing + 7 touch on 812×375 hasTouch).

**Why:** PWA made the game installable everywhere but mouse-only; chosen 2026-07-06 over IndexedDB saves and a content batch. **User decision: merge gates on automated tests only — the real-device pass is a fast-follow**, checklist lives in docs/testing.md ("Touch: the real-device checklist"); feel constants (`TOUCH_*` in config.ts, tuning.md "Touch feel") are educated guesses awaiting that pass.

**How to apply:**
- PR/push awaits the user. No protocol/save/worldgen impact; desktop byte-identical (existing e2e is the regression proof).
- e2e gotchas learned: Playwright `hasTouch` does NOT flip `(pointer: coarse)` → the `touchMode` fixture option seeds forced-on mode; gesture tests need the suite's 1 s settle (first-seconds chunk meshing jank swallows synthetic pointer moves — observed as partial/zero look deltas); wait for the overlay DOM after engage (the lock flag flips before React commits).
- Deferred (documented in README/manual/CHANGELOG): touch chat typing, F3, tap-a-block targeting, keybinding screen, mobile perf knobs (DPR 1.5 / render-radius).

PR #55's checks are still running (`verify` pending, CodeRabbit reviewing) — I'll report when they land. Now, the recommendation — and this time my honest answer is different from the last two rounds:

**Don't start a fourth feature yet. The next move is a consolidation pass.** Here's why: in two days you've shipped the PWA, melee lag compensation, and (pending merge) touch play — but three things have quietly piled up behind them:

1. **An unshipped release.** `main` carries two major unreleased features, soon three. That's a **v0.15.0** tag waiting to happen — and it's your biggest release since 0.13: installable, offline, lag-compensated, touch-playable. Minutes of work once #55 lands.
2. **Four pending manual passes**, all user-side, all verifiable in one sitting: the PWA pass on prod (install, offline session, Lighthouse), the two-browser lag-comp check (`setSimulatedLatency(300, 50)`, melee a walking mob), the ping re-test on the new sjc region (expect NA 60–100 ms, Asia 200–400 ms), and the touch real-device checklist (the big one — feel constants are educated guesses until a real thumb tries them). Automated tests said these features work; only these passes say they work *for players*. Shipping more before closing that loop inverts the pyramid.
3. **Touch feel tuning** will almost certainly fall out of the device pass — config-only by design, a quick follow-up commit.

**When you're ready for the next feature**, my pick is now **IndexedDB saves**: the PWA and touch play both multiply long-lived offline worlds on devices where cloud saves can't rescue anyone, so localStorage's ~5–10 MB quota cliff is currently the most likely way a real player loses progress. It's medium-sized (async storage layer + transparent one-time migration + quota tests) and the riskiest kind of change (save path), so it deserves a careful session of its own. The **content batch** stays the fun alternative, and the smaller deferred pool (arrow lag comp, touch chat, mobile perf knobs, binary tick packing) remains available as filler work.

One practical note: this session is at 73% context. The memory files are current — `touch-play-branch.md`, `lag-comp-branch.md`, and `pwa-branch.md` carry everything a fresh session needs — so I'd suggest: let me finish #55 (checks + CodeRabbit triage + merge + tag v0.15.0 if you want it), then start IndexedDB saves in a fresh session, same as we did for the PWA handoff.
